verses.title: Obeisance to Sadguru
tr: Je swaroop samjya vina, pamyo dukh anant;
Samjavyu te pada namun, Shri Sadguru Bhagwant.
iast: Je svarūpa samajyā vinā, pāmyo duḥkha anaṁta;
Samajāvyuṁ te pada namuṁ, Śrī Sadguru Bhagavaṁta.
gu: જે સ્વરૂપ સમજ્યા વિના, પામ્યો દુઃખ અનંત;
સમજાવ્યું તે પદ નમું, શ્રી સદ્ગુરુ ભગવંત.
link: As per the tradition of giving anubandh chatushtay, Param Krupalu Dev has woven it in two verses with excellent proficiency.
In the first verse, He has explained the auspicious and relation and in the second verse, the subject and the purpose.
At the commencement of the Shastra, aligning with the ancient tradition, paying obeisance to His Sadguru, He says -
words: I bow at the Feet of / Salutations
Enlightened Mentor who is Divine Guru and God
short: The Soul has been enduring sorrow since infinite time, without realising the nature of the Self.
I humbly bow to the Enlightened Mentor, who made me understand that nature of the Self.

verses.title: Subject and Purpose
tr: Vartman aa kaalma, mokshmarg bahu lop;
Vicharva atmarthine, bhakhyo atra agopya.
iast: Vartamāna ā kāḷamāṁ, mokṣamārga bahu lopa;
Vicāravā ātmārthīne, bhākhyo atra agopya.
gu: વર્તમાન આ કાળમાં, મોક્ષમાર્ગ બહુ લોપ;
વિચારવા આત્માર્થીને, ભાખ્યો અત્ર અગોપ્ય.
link: Aligning with the ancient tradition of Great spiritual composers - Param Krupalu Dev paid obeisance to the benevolent Sadguru Bhagwan.
In this verse, weaving the remaining two aspects namely - the subject of the text and the purpose; He says -
words: Clearly shown without concealing (hiding), without any reservations
short: The path of liberation has, by and large become extinct in the present times (era).
It has been clearly shown (stated) here explicitly (without any reservations / hiding).
For the contemplation of true aspirants of Self-realisation.

verses.title: Two Types of Deluded People
tr: Koi kriyajada thai rahya, shushkjnanma koi;
Maane marag mokshno, karuna upje joi.
iast: Koī kriyājaḍa thaī rahyā, śuṣkajñānamāṁ koī;
Māne māraga mokṣano, karuṇā ūpaje joī.
gu: કોઈ ક્રિયાજડ થઈ રહ્યા, શુષ્કજ્ઞાનમાં કોઈ;
માને મારગ મોક્ષનો, કરુણા ઊપજે જોઈ.
link: Before revealing the true path of liberation Param Krupalu Dev is now pointing out the prevailing wrong beliefs and conduct regarding the path of liberation.
In this verse - Param Krupalu Dev gives a tragic picture of why the path seems disappeared in the present times. He says -
words: Engrossed in rituals and external activities only
short: Some people have become staunch ritualist.
Others are having barren theoretical knowledge.
Compassion arises for both of them - mechanical ritualist and dry intellectualist.
As they believe themselves to be on the path of liberation.

verses.title: Characteristics of Mechanical Ritualist
tr: Bahya kriyama rachta, antarbhed na kai;
Jnanmarg nishedhta, the kriyajada aai.
iast: Bāhya kriyāmāṁ rācatā, aṁtarbheda na kaṁī;
Jñānamārga niṣedhatā, teha kriyājaḍa āṁī.
gu: બાહ્ય ક્રિયામાં રાચતા, અંતર્ભેદ ન કંઈ;
જ્ઞાનમાર્ગ નિષેધતા, તેહ ક્રિયાજડ આંઈ.
link: In order that both the category of people realise their mistake and others do not get carried away, Param Krupalu Dev explains the traits of both.
In this verse, for easy recognition of a kriyajada by describing its characteristics so that they can correct it and move forward on the path of liberation. He says -
words: He is / such indeed is a
short: The staunch ritualist is content with physical ritualistic activities (lifeless rituals).
He doesn’t differentiate between the body and the soul (so losing sight of their spiritual significance).
Negates the path of knowledge (wisdom) regarding it unnecessary and difficult.

verses.title: Characteristics of Dry Intellectualist
tr: Bandh moksh chhe kalpana, bhakhe vani mahi;
Varte mohaveshma, shushkjnani te aahi.
iast: Baṁdha mokṣa che kalpanā, bhākhe vāṇī māṁhī;
Varte mohāveśamāṁ, śuṣkajñānī te āṁhī.
gu: બંધ મોક્ષ છે કલ્પના, ભાખે વાણી માંહી;
વર્તે મોહાવેશમાં, શુષ્કજ્ઞાની તે આંહી.
link: After having shown the nature of kriyajada.
In this verse - Param Krupalu Dev described the nature of a shushkjnani; so that those who have such traits can give them up and make progress in the right way on the path of liberation. He says -
words: Dry intellectualist / hollow intellectualist barren scholar / one with superfluous knowledge
short: A person having barren knowledge lives in delusion.
He calls bondage and liberation of the soul as an illusion.
They speak in words, but their life is full of delusions and are victims of infatuations.
Thereby degenerating morally and spiritually.

verses.title: Benefits of Spiritual Practices
tr: Vairagyadi safal to, jo sah atamjnan;
Tem j atamjnanni, praptitana nidan.
iast: Vairāgyādi saphaḷa to, jo saha ātamajñāna;
Tema ja ātamajñānanī, prāptitaṇāṁ nidāna.
gu: વૈરાગ્યાદિ સફળ તો, જો સહ આતમજ્ઞાન;
તેમ જ આતમજ્ઞાનની, પ્રાપ્તિતણાં નિદાન.
link: Having described the nature of mechanical ritualist and dry intellectualist.
Now in verse 6 and 7, Param Krupalu Dev establishes the importance of renunciation and detachment, to join both the groups on the path of liberation. He says -
short: Detachment and other pure feelings like renunciation, compassion, charity etc. are fruitful if accompanied with experiential knowledge of the soul (Self-realisation).
They are also the means for Self-realisation; if practised for the sole reason to achieve it.

verses.title: Importance of Spiritual Practices
tr: Tyag virag na chittma, thay na tene jnan;
Atke tyag viragma, to bhule nijbhan.
iast: Tyāga virāga na cittamāṁ, thāya na tene jñāna;
Aṭake tyāga virāgamāṁ, to bhūle nijabhāna.
gu: ત્યાગ વિરાગ ન ચિત્તમાં, થાય ન તેને જ્ઞાન;
અટકે ત્યાગ વિરાગમાં, તો ભૂલે નિજભાન.
link: After explaining the importance of renunciation / detachment etc. before the dawn of Self-realisation, He is now reinforcing it.
Showing the necessity and the benefits of them to mechanical ritualists and dry intellectualists He says -
short: One cannot attain enlightenment without having feelings of renunciation and detachment within him (in his heart).
One also cannot attain enlightenment if he feels satisfied and forgets his Self-awareness.

verses.title: Virtue of Prudence
tr: Jya jya je je yogya chhe, taha samajvu teh;
Tya tya te te achare, atmarthi jan eh.
iast: Jyāṁ jyāṁ je je yogya che, tahāṁ samajavuṁ teha;
Tyāṁ tyāṁ te te ācare, ātmārthī jana eha.
gu: જ્યાં જ્યાં જે જે યોગ્ય છે, તહાં સમજવું તેહ;
ત્યાં ત્યાં તે તે આચરે, આત્માર્થી જન એહ.
link: After describing the traits of kriyajada and shushkjnani in verses 3 - 7.
Now in this verse, He explains the nature of a true aspirant - seeker of Self-realisation. He says -
words: Is worthy of adoption / is appropriate
short: One who understands everything in its appropriate context and acts accordingly.
Is a true seeker of the soul.
(The wise seeker adopts and practises renunciation etc. wherever it is fit to be practised - i.e. he lays the right degree of emphasis on the external modes of Self-realisation.)

verses.title: Sadguru is Essential
tr: Seve Sadguru Charanne, tyagi dai nijpaksh;
Pamey te parmarthne, nijpadno le laksh.
iast: Seve Sadgurucaraṇane, tyāgī daī nijapakṣa;
Pāme te paramārthane, nijapadano le lakṣa.
gu: સેવે સદ્ગુરુચરણને, ત્યાગી દઈ નિજપક્ષ;
પામે તે પરમાર્થને, નિજપદનો લે લક્ષ.
link: After showing the attributes of a true seeker (atmarthi) - now from verses 9 - 20 - He explains the necessity of a Sadguru.
In this verse, describing who can get his focus on the Self; He says -
words: The Feet of an Enlightened Mentor / True Teacher
short: One who serves the Feet of the Sadguru (Enlightened Mentor), giving up his own opinions.
Realises the supreme truth and attains the goal of Self-realisation.

verses.title: Qualities of Sadguru
tr: Atmajnan samdarshita, vichare udayprayog;
Apurva vani paramshrut, Sadguru lakshan yogya.
iast: Ātmajñāna samadarśitā, vicare udayaprayoga;
Apūrva vāṇī paramaśruta, Sadguru lakṣaṇa yogya.
gu: આત્મજ્ઞાન સમદર્શિતા, વિચરે ઉદયપ્રયોગ;
અપૂર્વ વાણી પરમશ્રુત, સદ્ગુરુ લક્ષણ યોગ્ય.
link: The association of a Sadguru is a straight, simple and short way of getting the right guidance for the path of liberation.
However, the seeker is safe only if he has a true Guru. Therefore it is necessary to identify a Sadguru. So in this verse, He gives the characteristics of a true Guru. He says -
words: Lives according to the past karmas
short: The admirable qualities of a True Teacher are - Self-realisation, equanimity, all actions are due to the operation of past karmas, unprecedented unique speech and knowledge of scriptures.

verses.title: Importance of Living Sadguru
tr: Pratyaksh Sadguru sam nahi, paroksh Jina upkar;
Evo laksh thaya vina, uge na atmavichar.
iast: Pratyakṣa Sadguru sama nahīṁ, parokṣa Jina upakāra;
Evo lakṣa thayā vinā, ūge na ātmavicāra.
gu: પ્રત્યક્ષ સદ્ગુરુ સમ નહીં, પરોક્ષ જિન ઉપકાર;
એવો લક્ષ થયા વિના, ઊગે ન આત્મવિચાર.
link: After showing the qualities of a True Teacher (Guru).
In this verse, He shows how necessary it is to have a living Sadguru. He says -
words: Self-contemplation / think correctly about the Self
short: The basic thought process of the soul does not arise, until one realises.
That the obligation of a living Enlightened Mentor is greater than the obligations of a non-present Omniscient God.

verses.title: Benevolence of Sadguru
tr: Sadguruna updesh van, samjay na jinroop;
Samjya van upkar sho? Samjye Jinswaroop.
iast: Sadgurunā upadeśa vaṇa, samajāya na Jinarūpa;
Samajyā vaṇa upakāra śo? Samajye Jinasvarūpa.
gu: સદ્ગુરુના ઉપદેશ વણ, સમજાય ન જિનરૂપ;
સમજ્યા વણ ઉપકાર શો? સમજ્યે જિનસ્વરૂપ.
link: Having shown the importance of the living Sadguru (pratyaksh Sadguru).
Now shows His exceptional benevolence. He says -
words: The true nature of the Jinas (Conquerers)
How can any good be derived
Then alone it is possible to comprehend
The true nature of the Jinas
short: One cannot understand the nature of Jineshwar Bhagwan, without the preaching of an Enlightened Mentor (Sadguru).
What benefit could be derived by a soul without this understanding?
One can comprehend and attain the true nature of the Jina only with such understanding.

verses.title: In Absence of Sadguru
tr: Atmadi astitvana, jeh nirupak shastra;
Pratyaksh Sadguru yog nahi, tya adhar supatra.
iast: Ātmādi astitvanāṁ, jeha nirūpaka śāstra;
Pratyakṣa Sadguru yoga nahi, tyāṁ ādhāra supātra.
gu: આત્માદિ અસ્તિત્વનાં, જેહ નિરૂપક શાસ્ત્ર;
પ્રત્યક્ષ સદ્ગુરુ યોગ નહિ, ત્યાં આધાર સુપાત્ર.
link: In verse 11 and 12, He clearly stated that the pratyaksh Sadguru is the ultimate refuge in the attainment of Self-realisation.
In this verse, He guides us - what to do if a qualified seeker cannot find a pratyaksh Sadguru, who is the ultimate benefactor. He says -
words: That which explain this / establish this
short: When there is absence of an Enlightened Living Mentor, the scriptures.
Which deal with the existence of soul and non-soul.
Are the sustainer and authentic guides.
Can be relied upon by deserving souls.
(But they do not have the capacity of an Enlightened Living Guru for removing seekers’ delusion.)

verses.title: When Continuous Association is not Possible
tr: Athva Sadgurue kahya, je avgahan kaj;
Te te nitya vicharva, kari matantar tyaj.
iast: Athavā Sadgurue kahyāṁ, je avagāhana kāja;
Te te nitya vicāravāṁ, karī matāṁtara tyāja.
gu: અથવા સદ્ગુરુએ કહ્યાં, જે અવગાહન કાજ;
તે તે નિત્ય વિચારવાં, કરી મતાંતર ત્યાજ.
link: He who has a pratyaksh Sadguru, but does not get to be in His company continuously.
In such a condition, what should be done? Giving guidance, now in this verse, He says -
words: Texts advised / guided / recommended by        the Sadguru
For the benefit of the soul
short: Or the texts recommended by the Enlightened Mentor should be studied.
Regularly giving up prejudices and dogmatism for the benefit of the soul.

verses.title: Refrain From Self-Will
tr: Roke jiva swachhand to, pamey avashya moksh;
Pamya em anant chhe, bhakhyu Jina nirdosh.
iast: Roke jīva svacchaṁda to, pāme avaśya mokṣa;
Pāmyā ema anaṁta che, bhākhyuṁ Jina nirdoṣa.
gu: રોકે જીવ સ્વચ્છંદ તો, પામે અવશ્ય મોક્ષ;
પામ્યા એમ અનંત છે, ભાખ્યું જિન નિર્દોષ.
link: In verses 9 - 14, He clearly stated that the path of liberation is dependent on pratyaksh Sadguru.
By being in the state of devotion, ones’ flaws like swachhand (self- will) gets easily destroyed.
This is described in 4 verses - 15 - 18. He says in this verse -
words: If the soul gets free of
short: Faultless Pure Jineshwar Bhagwan has said.
That a soul can surely attain liberation.
Only if the soul gets free of self-willed behaviour.
In the past, infinite souls have thus attained liberation.

verses.title: Remedy to Remove Self-Will
tr: Pratyaksh Sadguru yogthi, swachhand te rokay;
Anya upay karya thaki, praye bamano thay.
iast: Pratyakṣa Sadguru yogathī, svacchaṁda te rokāya;
Anya upāya karyā thakī, prāye bamaṇo thāya.
gu: પ્રત્યક્ષ સદ્ગુરુ યોગથી, સ્વચ્છંદ તે રોકાય;
અન્ય ઉપાય કર્યા થકી, પ્રાયે બમણો થાય.
link: Knowing that swachhand is the biggest hindrance on the path of liberation,
In this verse, showing how to get rid of it, He says -
words: Becomes double / will multiply      Becomes manifold stronger
short: The self-willed behaviour / attitude is restrained in the presence of an Enlightened Mentor.
Mostly, without an Enlightened Mentor swachhand will multiply.
It would only lead to a higher level of swachhand and becomes stronger.

verses.title: Benefit of Eliminating Self-Will
tr: Swachhand, mat agrah taji, varte Sadgurulaksh;
Samkit tene bhakhiyu, karan gani pratyaksh.
iast: Svacchaṁda, mata āgraha tajī, varte Sadgurulakṣa;
Samakita tene bhākhiyuṁ, kāraṇa gaṇī pratyakṣa.
gu: સ્વચ્છંદ, મત આગ્રહ તજી, વર્તે સદ્ગુરુલક્ષ;
સમકિત તેને ભાખિયું, કારણ ગણી પ્રત્યક્ષ.
link: What state does one attain if he eliminates swachhand - the greatest flaw, by taking refuge of a pratyaksh Sadguru and living in accordance with His intent.
He explains in this verse -
words: Strictly obeys the guidance of a true Guru
Knowing it is the obvious cause
short: The person who follows the preachings of the Enlightened Mentor, and gives up swachhand etc. in supporting his wrong views,
He is said to have right belief, as this is known to be the direct / obvious cause for right belief.

verses.title: Vanquishing Deadly Foes
tr: Maanadik shatru maha, nij chhande na maray;
Jata Sadguru sharanma, alp prayase jaay.
iast: Mānādika śatru mahā, nija chaṁde na marāya;
Jātāṁ Sadguru śaraṇamāṁ, alpa prayāse jāya.
gu: માનાદિક શત્રુ મહા, નિજ છંદે ન મરાય;
જાતાં સદ્ગુરુ શરણમાં, અલ્પ પ્રયાસે જાય.
link: Giving an easy and unfailing way to destroy the enemies like ego etc. that hinder the spiritual growth,
He says -
words: By himself / by his own efforts
Under the protection / shelter of a True Guru
short: Pride and other passions are the biggest enemies of the soul as they hinder the spiritual growth.
They cannot be destroyed by one's own efforts.
By seeking refuge of the Enlightened Mentor, they get destroyed by little effort.

verses.title: Importance of Humility
tr: Je Sadguru updeshthi, pamyo kevaljnan;
Guru rahya chhadmasth pan, vinay karey Bhagwan.
iast: Je Sadguru upadeśathī, pāmyo kevaḷajñāna;
Guru rahyā chadmastha paṇa, vinaya kare Bhagavāna.
gu: જે સદ્ગુરુ ઉપદેશથી, પામ્યો કેવળજ્ઞાન;
ગુરુ રહ્યા છદ્મસ્થ પણ, વિનય કરે ભગવાન.
link: With the help of the Sadguru, one can destroy flaws like swachhand. Explaining this in verses 15 - 18, highlighted the greatness of the refuge of the benevolent Sadguru.
Depicting the kind of humility, a worthy disciple has towards a Sadguru, He says -
words: By the preaching of a True Guru
short: A disciple may attain omniscient knowledge by imbibing the preaching of the Enlightened Mentor.
Even when the Master has not attained omniscience / absolute knowledge.
Even then, the omniscient (disciple) respects the Enlightened Master - continues to pay respects to His Guru.

verses.title: Path of Humility
tr: Evo marg vinay tano, bhakhyo Shri Vitrag;
Mool hetu e margno, samje koi subhagya.
iast: Evo mārga vinaya taṇo, bhākhyo Śrī Vītarāga;
Mūḷa hetu e mārgano, samaje koī subhāgya.
gu: એવો માર્ગ વિનય તણો, ભાખ્યો શ્રી વીતરાગ;
મૂળ હેતુ એ માર્ગનો, સમજે કોઈ સુભાગ્ય.
link: Having shown the zenith of humility,
Shedding more light on the subject of the path of humility, He says -
short: The path of reverence has been revealed by the Omniscient God, who are completely non-attached,
Only some fortunate soul can understand the main purpose and the immense benefits of such a path.

verses.title: Fate of Fake Guru
tr: Asadguru e vinayno, laabh lahey jo kai;
Mahamohniya karmathi, bude bhavjal mahi.
iast: Asadguru e vinayano, lābha lahe jo kāṁī;
Mahāmohanīya karmathī, būḍe bhavajaḷa māṁhī.
gu: અસદ્ગુરુ એ વિનયનો, લાભ લહે જો કાંઈ;
મહામોહનીય કર્મથી, બૂડે ભવજળ માંહી.
link: The supremely beneficial path of humility must be followed towards a Sadguru endowed with virtues.
Without this eligibility, an asadguru cannot be helpful to anyone spiritually. Explaining the fate of an asadguru, He says -
words: In the ocean of cycles of birth and death
short: If a person acting as an Enlightened Mentor, takes any advantage of such reverence.
He sinks in the ocean of infinite cycles of birth and death by being bound with intense deluding karma.
(Because such a teacher misleads the disciple therefore it is doubly harmful.)

verses.title: Necessity of Right Interpretation
tr: Hoy mumukshu jiva te, samje eh vichar;
Hoy matarthi jiva te, avlo le nirdhar.
iast: Hoya mumukṣu jīva te, samaje eha vicāra;
Hoya matārthī jīva te, avaḷo le nirdhāra.
gu: હોય મુમુક્ષુ જીવ તે, સમજે એહ વિચાર;
હોય મતાર્થી જીવ તે, અવળો લે નિર્ધાર.
link: An asadguru is one who is ignorant and claims to be a Guru.
One who wishes to learn the path from such an asadguru is a bigot (matarthi), making that clear, He says -
short: The soul desirous of liberation understands the concept (nature and purpose) of reverence revealed by the Jinas and Masters.
The soul who is a bigot misunderstands the concept of reverence, draws wrong conclusions.
Bigot = fanatic, sectarian
Deluded soul absorbed in its own whims.
Obstinately convinced by his own opinions.
Prejudiced against those who hold different opinions.

verses.title: Characteristics of Bigot
tr: Hoy matarthi tehne, thay na atamlaksh;
Teh matarthi lakshano, ahi kahya nirpaksh.
iast: Hoya matārthī tehane, thāya na ātamalakṣa;
Teha matārthī lakṣaṇo, ahīṁ kahyāṁ nirpakṣa.
gu: હોય મતાર્થી તેહને, થાય ન આતમલક્ષ;
તેહ મતાર્થી લક્ષણો, અહીં કહ્યાં નિર્પક્ષ.
link: A bigot (matarthi) does not understand the purpose of the path of humility, so no matter how much efforts he puts, the basic error remains intact.
Depicting the outcome of such behaviour of a bigot, He says -
words: Has no inclination to soul knowledge / awareness
I describe / stated here / will be showing now
short: A bigot will not attain Self-realisation.
The characteristics of such a bigot are stated here (hence) (in the following verses 24-33).
Without any prejudice or selfish motive.

verses.title: Bigot’s Belief Regarding Sadguru
tr: Bahyatyag pan jnan nahi, te maney Guru satya;
Athva nijkuldharmna, te Guruma j mamatva.
iast: Matārthī-lakṣaṇa Bāhyatyāga paṇa jñāna nahi, te māne guru satya;
Athavā nijakuḷadharmanā, te Gurumāṁ ja mamatva.
gu: મતાર્થી-લક્ષણ બાહ્યત્યાગ પણ જ્ઞાન નહિ, તે માને ગુરુ સત્ય;
અથવા નિજકુળધર્મના, તે ગુરુમાં જ મમત્વ.
link: Describing the nature of a kriyajada matarthi who is under the illusion that he is practising right conduct, in 5 verses, Param Krupalu Dev throws light on his false beliefs regarding Dev-Guru- Dharma, the supreme benevolent factors of spiritual welfare.
In the first verse, depicting the matarthi’s false beliefs regarding the Guru, Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: Of his own birth - ancestors - forefathers religion / his family Guru
short: A bigot, one whose approach is sectarian, believes that a person with external renunciation but no Self-realisation is fit to be a true Guru (though no inner detachment and enlightenment).
Alternately, he believes in a person being followed by his forefathers, as true Guru. He must be convinced that he is enlightened or search of a true Guru will stop, or not even start.

verses.title: Bigot’s Belief Regarding God
tr: Je Jindeh praman ne, samvasaranadi siddhi;
Varnan samje Jinnu, roki rahey nij buddhi.
iast: Je Jinadeha pramāṇa ne, samavasaraṇādi siddhi;
Varṇana samaje Jinanuṁ, rokī rahe nija buddhi.
gu: જે જિનદેહ પ્રમાણ ને, સમવસરણાદિ સિદ્ધિ;
વર્ણન સમજે જિનનું, રોકી રહે નિજ બુદ્ધિ.
link: Just as a matarthi makes a mistake in recognising a Sadguru, will now describe the mistake he makes in understanding the true nature of Satdev (true God).
Pointing out the prevalent false beliefs regarding Satdev, Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: Size of the body of Omniscient God and
Gorgeous decorations of the assembly of Omniscient God etc.
Considers these descriptions as the nature
short: He understands the description of the body of the Omniscient God and the other outward appearance as the real description of Omniscient God, the Jinas.
He who confines his intelligence to such external manifestations and glory as the nature of Jinas is a religious bigot.

verses.title: Bigot’s Disregard for Sadguru
tr: Pratyaksh Sadguruyogma, varte drashti vimukh;
Asadgurune dradh karey, nij maanarthe mukhya.
iast: Pratyakṣa Sadguruyogamāṁ, varte dṛṣṭi vimukha;
Asadgurune dṛḍha kare, nija mānārthe mukhya.
gu: પ્રત્યક્ષ સદ્ગુરુયોગમાં, વર્તે દૃષ્ટિ વિમુખ;
અસદ્ગુરુને દૃઢ કરે, નિજ માનાર્થે મુખ્ય.
link: Verse 25 - explained the false belief regarding the nature of God.  Verse 24 - explained the false belief regarding the nature of Guru.
Now in this verse (26) - explains how a matarthi acts, despite finding a Sadguru. Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: Follows with determination / strengthens his faith in him
short: He behaves with perverse attitude in the presence of the Enlightened Mentor, when available - overlooks or disregards Him and
He follows the untrue teacher with faith mainly to gratify his own pride.
(To earn respect both from the imposter and the public attending on the imposter thereby he develops his pride and vanity.)

verses.title: Bigot’s Belief Regarding Dharma
tr: Devadi gati bhangma, je samje shrutjnan;
Maney nij mat veshno, agrah muktinidan.
iast: Devādi gati bhaṁgamāṁ, je samaje śrutajñāna;
Māne nija mata veṣano, āgraha muktinidāna.
gu: દેવાદિ ગતિ ભંગમાં, જે સમજે શ્રુતજ્ઞાન;
માને નિજ મત વેષનો, આગ્રહ મુક્તિનિદાન.
link: From verse 24 - 26 different aspects of false belief regarding the nature of Satguru and Satdev were explained.
Now in verse 27 - 28, prevailing false beliefs regarding the nature of religion are described.
In this verse, false belief regarding scriptures, and opinions regarding external attire are described. Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: Narrations of the classification / types of conditions of existence
Sectarian attire / adopted dress of his religion
short: He believes that the narration of classification of celestial or heavenly beings etc. is the scriptural knowledge, which leads to Self-realisation.
He regards the insistence of outward dress of his own religion (sectarian attire) as the cause of liberation.

verses.title: Bigot’s Belief Regarding Dharma
tr: Lahyu swaroop na vruttinu, grahyu vrat abhiman;
Grahe nahi parmarthne, leva laukik maan.
iast: Lahyuṁ svarūpa na vṛttinuṁ, grahyuṁ vrata abhimāna;
Grahe nahīṁ paramārthane, levā laukika māna.
gu: લહ્યું સ્વરૂપ ન વૃત્તિનું, ગ્રહ્યું વ્રત અભિમાન;
ગ્રહે નહીં પરમાર્થને, લેવા લૌકિક માન.
link: Having shown the false belief about the nature of dharma - regarding scriptures and opinions regarding the external attire as cause of liberation.
Now showing the wrong notions regarding the components of dharma such as vows (austerities) Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: Neither understand the nature nor control the
With a view to earn respect from others
Worldly position / attention / honour People’s respect for him
short: He does not understand the nature of inner intent process of renunciation and vows, and
Takes pride for the vows taken by him.
He is focussed on achieving worldly position and misses out on supreme truth.

verses.title: Bigot Forsakes Means of Liberation
tr: Athva nishchay naya grahe, matra shabdani maay;
Lope sadvyavharne, sadhan rahit thay.
iast: Athavā niścaya naya grahe, mātra śabdanī māṁya;
Lope sadvyavahārane, sādhana rahita thāya.
gu: અથવા નિશ્ચય નય ગ્રહે, માત્ર શબ્દની માંય;
લોપે સદ્વ્યવહારને, સાધન રહિત થાય.
link: From verse 24 - 28, Param Krupalu Dev explained the characteristics of a kriyajada matarthi (mechanical ritualist).
Now from verse 29 - 31 will explain the characteristics of a shushkjnani  matarthi (dry intellectualist).
Explaining the nature of a shushkjnani matarthi Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: Or
He adopts the absolute viewpoint.
Merely to the extent of speaking in words.
He neglects the good conducts and becomes devoid of the means of Self-realisation. (Accepts the description of the true nature of the Self but does not make any efforts to realise it.)

verses.title: Association of Bigot
tr: Jnandasha pamey nahi, sadhandasha na kai;
Pamey teno sang je, te bude bhav mahi.
iast: Jñānadaśā pāme nahīṁ, sādhanadaśā na kāṁī;
Pāme teno saṁga je, te būḍe bhava māṁhī.
gu: જ્ઞાનદશા પામે નહીં, સાધનદશા ન કાંઈ;
પામે તેનો સંગ જે, તે બૂડે ભવ માંહી.
link: Shushkjnani matarthi gives up the means that are instrumental in bringing his upliftment.
Now in the next two verses, is described how he forsakes his own good.
In this verse, showing the fate of those who associate with such matarthis, Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: Equipped with means / in right discipline
Who stay in the association of them
short: He does not attain Self-realisation and also does not practise the means.
A person who stays in his company (also),
Sinks in the ocean of infinite cycles of birth and death.

verses.title: Bigots Stand Disqualified
tr: E pan jiva matarthama, nijmaanadi kaaj;
Pamey nahi parmarthne, an-adhikarima j.
iast: E paṇa jīva matārthamāṁ, nijamānādi kāja;
Pāme nahi paramārthane, an-adhikārīmāṁ ja.
gu: એ પણ જીવ મતાર્થમાં, નિજમાનાદિ કાજ;
પામે નહિ પરમાર્થને, અન્-અધિકારીમાં જ.
link: The shushkjnani who is deluded cannot attain spiritual welfare.
Param Krupalu Dev considers such people as matarthis. Explaining that, He says -
words: Not worthy / don't deserve / unqualified / ineligible
short: This kind of soul is also stuck in bigotry like the mechanical ritualist as he takes pride in his viewpoint.
He does not attain the supreme state as he is unworthy of it.

None of them are fit to be a seeker of liberation as both are attached to their whims (opinions) and do all for vanity; both run after pride and personal fame and so they run in the direction counter to that of truth.] [

verses.title: Common Attributes of Bigots
tr: Nahi kashay upshantta, nahi antar vairagya;
Saralpanu na madhyasthata, e matarthi durbhagya.
iast: Nahi kaṣāya upaśāṁtatā, nahi aṁtara vairāgya;
Saraḷapaṇuṁ na madhyasthatā, e matārthī durbhāgya.
gu: નહિ કષાય ઉપશાંતતા, નહિ અંતર વૈરાગ્ય;
સરળપણું ન મધ્યસ્થતા, એ મતાર્થી દુર્ભાગ્ય.
link: From verse 24 - 31, Param Krupalu Dev described the distinct characteristics of the two types of matarthis - the kriyajada and the shushkjnani and showed how they both are unworthy for the attainment of the supreme truth.
In this verse, showing the common characteristics of both types of matarthis, Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: It is a misfortune of a bigot that he has
No subsidence of passion / have not been disarmed
No inner detachment / has not dawned
No simplicity / have not developed frankness
No impartiality / not have impartial insight
(For he can have no right faith and consequently no Self-knowledge for liberation.)

verses.title: Purpose of Explanation
tr: Lakshan kahya matarthina, matarth java kaaj;
Havey kahu atmarthina, atma-artha sukhsaaj.
iast: Lakṣaṇa kahyāṁ matārthīnāṁ, matārtha jāvā kāja;
Have kahuṁ ātmārthīnāṁ, ātma-artha sukhasāja.
gu: લક્ષણ કહ્યાં મતાર્થીનાં, મતાર્થ જાવા કાજ;
હવે કહું આત્માર્થીનાં, આત્મ-અર્થ સુખસાજ.
link: Thus in the earlier nine verses (24 - 32) Param Krupalu Dev explained in detail the attributes of the unfortunate ones who have gone astray from the true path.
Now, concluding the subject, in this verse, He shows the purpose behind describing the attributes of a matarthi and pledges to explain the attributes of an atmarthi. Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: The characteristics of a true seeker
Attainment of bliss of the soul
short: The characteristics of a bigot have been stated for the purpose of identifying and removing bigotry.
Now I will state the characteristics of a true seeker of the soul.
Whose sole purpose is inner bliss (Self-realisation).

verses.title: True Seeker’s Belief Regarding Sadguru
tr: Atmajnan tya munipanu, te sacha Guru hoy;
Baki kulguru kalpana, atmarthi nahi joy.
iast: Ātmārthī-lakṣaṇa Ātmajñāna tyāṁ munipaṇuṁ, te sācā Guru hoya;
Bākī kuḷaguru kalpanā, ātmārthī nahi joya.
gu: આત્માર્થી-લક્ષણ આત્મજ્ઞાન ત્યાં મુનિપણું, તે સાચા ગુરુ હોય;
બાકી કુળગુરુ કલ્પના, આત્માર્થી નહિ જોય.
link: In this section, attributes of a true seeker (atmarthi), Param Krupalu Dev describes the atmarthi’s belief regarding the most fundamental and important aspect - the nature of a true Guru (Sadguru).
Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: True monkhood / asceticism is where there is
To follow / worship teachers of one's own family tradition
short: The primary attribute of an atmarthi is the correct understanding of a true Sadguru.
He understands the importance of Self-realisation as a requisite of a Sadguru - true state of monkhood is not possible without Self-realisation.
Following a Guru of the family, who is ignorant (without Self- realisation) is delusional, not helpful in delivering him from cycles of birth and death.

verses.title: Living Sadguru is a Blessing
tr: Pratyaksh Sadguru praptino, ganey param upkar;
Trane yog ekatvathi, varte ajnadhar.
iast: Pratyakṣa Sadguru prāptino, gaṇe parama upakāra;
Traṇe yoga ekatvathī, varte ājñādhāra.
gu: પ્રત્યક્ષ સદ્ગુરુ પ્રાપ્તિનો, ગણે પરમ ઉપકાર;
ત્રણે યોગ એકત્વથી, વર્તે આજ્ઞાધાર.
link: Having explained what kind of Guru an atmarthi is devoted towards,
In this verse, Param Krupalu Dev describes the kind of devotion an atmarthi has towards Him, when he attains such a Sadguru. He says -
words: The energies of mind, speech, body
With the united activity / in unison
short: A true seeker of the soul considers the attainment of the living Enlightened Mentor as a unique opportunity; supremely beneficial to himself.
He surrenders to Him through all the three energies of mind (thought), speech (word) and body (deed).
And acts on His guidance - command - advice. Follows His ajna with inner devotion in every way.

verses.title: True Seeker’s Belief Regarding Path of Liberation
tr: Ek hoy tran kaalma, parmarathno panth;
Prere te parmarthne, te vyavhar samant.
iast: Eka hoya traṇa kāḷamāṁ, paramārathano paṁtha;
Prere te paramārthane, te vyavahāra samaṁta.
gu: એક હોય ત્રણ કાળમાં, પરમારથનો પંથ;
પ્રેરે તે પરમાર્થને, તે વ્યવહાર સમંત.
link: The atmarthi has utmost veneration for the Sadguru. Giving up self-will, he follows the ajna and makes earnest effort to pursue the path of liberation.
Throwing light on the atmarthi’s belief regarding the path of liberation, which forms the foundation of his desire to follow the path, Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: In past, present, future / in all times
Which is instrumental / inspires / leads to
To the path of supreme truth / liberation
short: There is only one path for achieving the supreme truth.
In the past, present and future.
One should accept, respect the practices which help lead to this one supreme truth. (Whichever practices lead the soul to liberation should be accepted, and no others.)

verses.title: Seek Sadguru with True Purpose
tr: Em vichari antare, shodhe Sadguru yog;
Kaam ek atmarthnu, bijo nahi mannrog.
iast: Ema vicārī aṁtare, śodhe Sadguru yoga;
Kāma eka ātmārthanuṁ, bījo nahi manaroga.
gu: એમ વિચારી અંતરે, શોધે સદ્ગુરુ યોગ;
કામ એક આત્માર્થનું, બીજો નહિ મનરોગ.
link: An atmarthi does not engage in practices that cannot annihilate the soul’s impure state. Instead he engages himself in cultivating virtues which bring worthiness in him.
Explaining what an atmarthi does for his spiritual welfare, Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: Thinking thus in the mind,
The true seeker searches for association of an Enlightened Mentor.
He has only one desire to attain Self-realisation and harbours no other desires (has no other mental cravings).
Spiritual welfare is the only goal of an atmarthi.

verses.title: Identity of True Seeker
tr: Kashayni upshantta, matra moksh abhilash;
Bhavey khed, pranidaya, tya atmarth nivas.
iast: Kaṣāyanī upaśāṁtatā, mātra mokṣa abhilāṣa;
Bhave kheda, prāṇīdayā, tyāṁ ātmārtha nivāsa.
gu: કષાયની ઉપશાંતતા, માત્ર મોક્ષ અભિલાષ;
ભવે ખેદ, પ્રાણીદયા, ત્યાં આત્માર્થ નિવાસ.
link: Spiritual welfare is the only goal of an atmarthi.

Throwing light on what type of a person has such a desire of spiritual welfare, Param Krupalu Dev describes the attributes of an atmarthi, as He had shown the common attributes of matarthi in verse - 32 in the section of matarthi. Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: Abode of Self-realisation / identity of a true seeker
short: There is the abode of Self-realisation.
Where there is -
Subsidence of passion (reducing worldly attachment).
Only desire of liberation (no other desire).
Grief for cycles of birth and death (reflects and removes his faults and flaws).
Compassion for all living beings (sympathy for all).
When an aspirant has developed these attributes he is considered a true seeker, can proceed in search of truth (these are the requisites of truth seekers).

verses.title: Need to Attain Worthiness
tr: Dasha na evi jya sudhi, jiva lahey nahi jog;
Mokshmarg pamey nahi, matey na antar rog.
iast: Daśā na evī jyāṁ sudhī, jīva lahe nahi joga;
Mokṣamārga pāme nahīṁ, maṭe na aṁtara roga.
gu: દશા ન એવી જ્યાં સુધી, જીવ લહે નહિ જોગ;
મોક્ષમાર્ગ પામે નહીં, મટે ન અંતર રોગ.
link: Until one attains such a state of worthiness, he is not qualified to attain the experience of the pure Self.
Thus, by using the method of negative assertion, Param Krupalu Dev says -
words: Of the association of a Sadguru
short: So long as the soul does not attain such a state of worthiness (as stated in verse - 38).
Cannot take the advantage of the association of a Sadguru and other favourable circumstances.
He does not attain the path of liberation and
His inner disease of self-delusion (ignorance of the nature of the Self) also does not get cured.

verses.title: Worthiness Leads to Right Thinking
tr: Aavey jya evi dasha, Sadgurubodh suhay;
Te bodhe suvicharna, tya pragate sukhday.
iast: Āve jyāṁ evī daśā, Sadgurubodha suhāya;
Te bodhe suvicāraṇā, tyāṁ pragaṭe sukhadāya.
gu: આવે જ્યાં એવી દશા, સદ્ગુરુબોધ સુહાય;
તે બોધે સુવિચારણા, ત્યાં પ્રગટે સુખદાય.
link: After describing the state of a worthy seeker through the method of negative assertion, now Param Krupalu Dev
Establishes the state of a worthy one through method of positive assertion.
Showing what happens when one attains the state of an atmarthi, Param Krupalu Dev describes the sequence of attaining the path. He says -
short: When the soul attains such a state.
The preachings of the Enlightened Mentor bear fruits, become effective - rightly interpreted and adopted.
That state leads to the state of true bliss.
Because the disciple turns his mind from worldly thoughts to contemplation and meditation on the nature of the Self and gets glimpses of the souls bliss.

verses.title: Right Thinking Leads to Liberation
tr: Jya pragate suvicharna, tya pragate nij jnan;
Je jnane kshay moh thai, pamey pada nirvan.
iast: Jyāṁ pragaṭe suvicāraṇā, tyāṁ pragaṭe nija jñāna;
Je jñāne kṣaya moha thaī, pāme pada nirvāṇa.
gu: જ્યાં પ્રગટે સુવિચારણા, ત્યાં પ્રગટે નિજ જ્ઞાન;
જે જ્ઞાને ક્ષય મોહ થઈ, પામે પદ નિર્વાણ.
link: Having explained how the state of right thinking emerges in an atmarthi,
Now explaining what the fruit of that right thinking is, that is, what happens after right thinking develops. Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: When the right thought process arises,
In him Self-realisation arises,
This Self-realisation results in annihilation of delusion and the soul attains liberation from cycles of birth and death.
With the contemplation on the nature of the Self comes Self-realisation which removes infatuation and ignorance and the soul attains liberation.) (

verses.title: Six Truths for Right Thinking
tr: Upje te suvicharna, mokshmarg samjay;
Gurushishyasamvadthi, bhakhu shatpad aahi.
iast: Ūpaje te suvicāraṇā, mokṣamārga samajāya;
Guruśiṣyasaṁvādathī, bhākhuṁ ṣaṭpada āṁhī.
gu: ઊપજે તે સુવિચારણા, મોક્ષમાર્ગ સમજાય;
ગુરુશિષ્યસંવાદથી, ભાખું ષટ્પદ આંહી.
link: Param Krupalu Dev commenced the description of the attributes of an atmarthi from verse - 34, which He now concludes in this verse - 42.
He clearly stated that the right mindset marks the beginning of the true seeker and when the state develops completely he attains liberation.
He now refers to the fundamentals, an atmarthi must know to attain the state of right thinking. He says -
words: In the form of dialogue between the Mentor and the disciple
Here as six aphorisms / six fundamental truths
short: In order to initiate the right thought process, which leads to the understanding of the path of liberation.
I state here six aphorisms in the form of dialogue between the Enlightened Mentor and the disciple.

verses.title: Naming Six Fundamental Truths
tr: ‘Atma chhe’, ‘Te nitya chhe’, ‘Chhe karta nijkarma’;
‘Chhe bhokta’, vali ‘Moksh chhe’, ‘Moksh upay sudharma’.
iast: ‘Ātmā che’, ‘Te nitya che’, ‘Che kartā nijakarma’;
‘Che bhoktā’, vaḷī ‘Mokṣa che’, ‘Mokṣa upāya sudharma’.
gu: ‘આત્મા છે’, ‘તે નિત્ય છે’, ‘છે કર્તા નિજકર્મ’;
‘છે ભોક્તા’, વળી ‘મોક્ષ છે’, ‘મોક્ષ ઉપાય સુધર્મ’.
link: As an introduction of the main subject of the text, Param Krupalu Dev has composed this section as ‘naming of the six fundamentals’ comprising of 2 verses.
In verse - 42, He indicated that He would explain the six fundamentals for reflection upon the Self. Naming these six fundamentals, He says -
words: It is the doer of its actions (karmas)
It is the enjoyer / endurer / receiver of its consequences
There is a path of liberation
short: The soul exists, it is eternal, it is doer of karmas, it is the enjoyer / endurer / receiver of fruits of karma, there is liberation. The path of liberation, which is true religion exists.
(A true religion liberates the soul from the worldly cycle of birth and death.)

verses.title: Purpose of Explaining Six Fundamental Truths
tr: Shatsthanak sankshepma, shatdarshan pan teh;
Samjava parmarthne, kahya Jnanie eh.
iast: Ṣaṭsthānaka saṁkṣepamāṁ, ṣaṭdarśana paṇa teha;
Samajāvā paramārthane, kahyāṁ jñānīe eha.
gu: ષટ્સ્થાનક સંક્ષેપમાં, ષટ્દર્શન પણ તેહ;
સમજાવા પરમાર્થને, કહ્યાં જ્ઞાનીએ એહ.
link: The six fundamentals were named in verse - 43.
Before commencing their detailed description in the form of dialogue between a Sadguru and sushishya, Param Krupalu Dev composed one more introductory verse.
Showing that it also explains the gist of 6 major philosophies as well as the purpose of explaining these six fundamentals, He says -
words: Six main philosophies / six schools of thought
short: These six aphorisms are stated here briefly.
They also constitute the six types of philosophies.

The Enlightened Ones have stated them to make us understand the supreme truth. (The six truths mentioned above also include a critical appreciation of the six systems of philosophy. These truths have been explained by the Enlightened Ones to understand the nature of ultimate reality.)

verses.title: Doubt 1 - Soul Cannot be Experienced by Senses
tr: Nathi drashtima aavto, nathi janatu roop;
Bijo pan anubhav nahi, tethi na jivswaroop.
iast: (1) Śaṁkā - śiṣya uvāca Nathī dṛṣṭimāṁ āvato, nathī jaṇātuṁ rūpa;
Bījo paṇa anubhava nahīṁ, tethī na jīvasvarūpa.
gu: (૧) શંકા - શિષ્ય ઉવાચ નથી દૃષ્ટિમાં આવતો, નથી જણાતું રૂપ;
બીજો પણ અનુભવ નહીં, તેથી ન જીવસ્વરૂપ.
link: To accept the existence of soul is the first step of the path of liberation. Therefore, it is important to be doubtless about it. For this fundamental Param Krupalu Dev has composed 14 verses (45 - 58).
In the first 4 verses (45 - 48), Param Krupalu Dev has presented the disciple's doubts regarding the existence of the soul which have arisen due to the influence of the atheistic Charvaka philosophy.
Presenting the first argument (without naming the Charvaka philosophy), He says -
words: Cannot be experienced by any other senses
short: The soul cannot be seen by eyes.
It has no form - its form is unknown.
There is no other way of experiencing it by any senses.
Therefore, the soul does not exist.
(The soul cannot be seen, known or experienced. It is only spoken of, but does not exist.)

verses.title: Doubt 2 - Soul is Body, Senses or Breath
tr: Athva deh j atama, athva indriya pran;
Mithya judo manvo, nahi judu endhan.
iast: Athavā deha ja ātamā, athavā indriya prāṇa;
Mithyā judo mānavo, nahīṁ juduṁ eṁdhāṇa.
gu: અથવા દેહ જ આતમા, અથવા ઇન્દ્રિય પ્રાણ;
મિથ્યા જુદો માનવો, નહીં જુદું એંધાણ.
link: Having expressed the reason of doubting the existence of the soul,
The disciple presents one more argument regarding that.
words: It's false to believe it separate from them
As there is no sign of its being separate
short: Or the soul is body itself,
Or it’s the senses and breath.
It is false to believe it to be separate from them.
There is no sign of it being separate from them (body, senses, breath).

verses.title: Doubt 3 - Soul is not Knowable Like Pot-Cloth
tr: Vali jo atma hoy to, janay te nahi kem?
Janay jo te hoy to, ghat pat adi jem.
iast: Vaḷī jo ātmā hoya to, jaṇāya te nahi kema?
Jaṇāya jo te hoya to, ghaṭa paṭa ādi jema.
gu: વળી જો આત્મા હોય તો, જણાય તે નહિ કેમ?
જણાય જો તે હોય તો, ઘટ પટ આદિ જેમ.
link: There is no distinct sign of the soul, therefore the disciple is not willing to accept the existence of the soul as separate from the body.
He puts forth another argument in this context.
words: Why is it not known / knowable
It would be known / if knowable
short: And if the soul exists, why is it not known?
If it exists, it should be known like pot, cloth etc.
(If the soul exists, as a substance then it should be felt by the senses as pots and clothes. But it cannot be perceived by any senses, hence it does not exist.)

verses.title: Concluding His Observations
tr: Matey chhe nahi atama, mithya moksh upay;
E antar shanka tano, samjavo sadupay.
iast: Māṭe che nahi ātamā, mithyā mokṣa upāya;
E aṁtara śaṁkā taṇo, samajāvo sadupāya.
gu: માટે છે નહિ આતમા, મિથ્યા મોક્ષ ઉપાય;
એ અંતર શંકા તણો, સમજાવો સદુપાય.
link: Through the arguments presented in verses 45 - 46 - 47, the disciple is inclined to believe that there is no substance like the soul, which has an independent existence.
Based on this belief, the disciple concludes that -
words: The means of liberation is useless
A satisfactory solution for the doubt in my mind
short: The soul, therefore does not exist.
The means of its liberation are therefore, useless.
Please give me a satisfactory solution for the doubt that I have in my mind.

(If religion is a method of soul’s liberation it is not required at all since the soul does not exist. O true Teacher, please remove my doubt and explain the nature of the soul’s existence if at all there is any.)

verses.title: Root Cause of Doubt
tr: Bhasyo dehadhyasthi, atma deh saman;
Pan te banne bhinna chhe, pragat lakshane bhan.
iast: (1) Samādhāna - Sadguru uvāca Bhāsyo dehādhyāsathī, ātmā deha samāna;
Paṇa te banne bhinna che, pragaṭa lakṣaṇe bhāna.
gu: (૧) સમાધાન - સદ્ગુરુ ઉવાચ ભાસ્યો દેહાધ્યાસથી, આત્મા દેહ સમાન;
પણ તે બન્ને ભિન્ન છે, પ્રગટ લક્ષણે ભાન.
link: The disciple presented his doubts regarding the existence of the soul to the Guru in the previous 4 verses (45 - 48).

Knowing the disciple to be worthy of knowledge, the Guru answers his doubts in 10 verses (49 - 58), as a result of this, his doubts are resolved and he develops faith in the first fundamental truth - the soul exists.

Before sequentially answering the various arguments of the disciple, the Guru draws his attention to the root cause of this doubt. In two verses, the Guru strikes on the basic flaw of all his doubts regarding existence of soul. He says -
short: The soul and the body appear as the same due to false identification of the soul with the body.
But both of them are separate entities and can be identified separately from their evident characteristics (obviously distinct).

verses.title: Root Cause of Doubt - Analogy
tr: Bhasyo dehadhyasthi, atma deh saman;
Pan te banne bhinna chhe, jem asi ne myan.
iast: Bhāsyo dehādhyāsathī, ātmā deha samāna;
Paṇa te banne bhinna che, jema asi ne myāna.
gu: ભાસ્યો દેહાધ્યાસથી, આત્મા દેહ સમાન;
પણ તે બન્ને ભિન્ન છે, જેમ અસિ ને મ્યાન.
link: Having shown that the soul is a substance that has an independent existence.
To further strengthen that conviction, the Sadguru repeats the first three parts of the previous verse and then clarifies that principle with an apt example. He says -
words: Like the sword and the sheath
short: The soul and the body appear same due to false identification.
But both of them are separate entities, like the sword and the sheath.

verses.title: Reply 1 - Soul is Seer
tr: Je drashta chhe drashtino, je janey chhe roop;
Abadhya anubhav je rahey, te chhe jivswaroop.
iast: Je draṣṭā che dṛṣṭino, je jāṇe che rūpa;
Abādhya anubhava je rahe, te che jīvasvarūpa.
gu: જે દ્રષ્ટા છે દૃષ્ટિનો, જે જાણે છે રૂપ;
અબાધ્ય અનુભવ જે રહે, તે છે જીવસ્વરૂપ.
link: After drawing the disciple’s attention towards the basic flaw which is the root cause of all his doubts regarding the soul.
The Guru gives precise answers to all the arguments one after the other, thus resolving all his doubts.

In this verse 51, the Guru answers the doubt raised by the disciple in verse 45 - the soul is not seen through eyes, its form or shape is not known, not known by other senses, therefore the soul does not exist.
Resolving this doubt of the disciple, the Guru says -
words: That which is knower of all forms
This is the nature / this is the characteristic       of the soul
short: That which is the seer of the sight and knower of all forms.
(It is the soul itself who is behind the eyes knowing the forms.)
The experience of consciousness, which is continuous, cannot be subtracted, independent of external objects is the nature of the soul (characteristic / sign).

verses.title: Knower of All Five Senses
tr: Chhe indriya pratyekne, nij nij vishaynu jnan;
Panch indrina vishaynu, pan atmane bhan.
iast: Che indriya pratyekane, nija nija viṣayanuṁ jñāna;
Pāṁca indrīnā viṣayanuṁ, paṇa ātmāne bhāna.
gu: છે ઇન્દ્રિય પ્રત્યેકને, નિજ નિજ વિષયનું જ્ઞાન;
પાંચ ઇન્દ્રીના વિષયનું, પણ આત્માને ભાન.
link: The Guru gave an accurate solution to the disciple’s argument expressed in verse 45, by saying that the nature of the soul cannot be perceived by the senses.
Explaining this further, kindling conviction about the soul through the attribute of knowledge, the Guru says -
words: Knowledge of its own subject matter (faculty)
Subject matter of all five senses
short: Each sense organ enables us to know only its faculty - ears cannot see, eyes cannot hear.
But the soul knows the subject matter of all five senses at one given time.
No sense can function without the soul.
It’s the coordinator and also remembers the experience in future.) (

verses.title: Reply 2 - Body, Sense, Breath Function Due to Soul
tr: Deh na janey tehne, janey na indri pran;
Atmani satta vadey, teh pravarte jaan.
iast: Deha na jāṇe tehane, jāṇe na indrī prāṇa;
Ātmānī sattā vaḍe, teha pravarte jāṇa.
gu: દેહ ન જાણે તેહને, જાણે ન ઇન્દ્રી પ્રાણ;
આત્માની સત્તા વડે, તેહ પ્રવર્તે જાણ.
link: After giving an apt solution to the argument presented by the disciple in verse 45, now the Guru resolves the doubt put forth in verse 46.
In verse 46, the disciple said that the body, senses or breath alone should be considered as the soul. There is no sign of existence of the soul separate from these.
The first half of this argument is resolved in verse 53 and the second half in verse 54.
Proving independent existence of the soul as separate from body, senses and breath, the Guru says -
words: The body does not know it
Nor do the senses and the breath
In the presence of the soul
short: The body does not know it.
The senses and the breath also do not know it.
The soul is the knower of the body, senses and the breath.
And they all function only due to the presence of the soul, else they lie inert.

verses.title: Consciousness is Sign of Soul
tr: Sarva avasthane vishe, nyaro sada janay;
Pragatroop chaitanyamay, e endhan saday.
iast: Sarva avasthāne viṣe, nyāro sadā jaṇāya;
Pragaṭarūpa caitanyamaya, e eṁdhāṇa sadāya.
gu: સર્વ અવસ્થાને વિષે, ન્યારો સદા જણાય;
પ્રગટરૂપ ચૈતન્યમય, એ એંધાણ સદાય.
link: The second part of the disciple's argument in verse 46 was that there is no sign of the soul evidently known, therefore, to believe it as separate from the body etc. is false.
Answering that, in this verse 54, the Guru says -
words: Is the characteristic of the soul
short: Though present in all the states (waking, dream, sleep) that which remains separate from those states,
Which continues to exist even after those states are gone and which knows those states,
Such is its evident nature of consciousness that is, to keep knowing is its evident nature and the sign is always present. The sign is never destroyed.

verses.title: Reply 3 - Knowledge Establishes Knower
tr: Ghat, pat adi jaan tu, tethi tene maan;
Jananar te maan nahi, kahie kevu jnan?
iast: Ghaṭa, paṭa ādi jāṇa tuṁ, tethī tene māna;
Jāṇanāra te māna nahi, kahīe kevuṁ jñāna?
gu: ઘટ, પટ આદિ જાણ તું, તેથી તેને માન;
જાણનાર તે માન નહિ, કહીએ કેવું જ્ઞાન?
link: In verse - 47, the disciple had presented the argument that if the soul does exist, then why is it not known the way pot, cloth etc. are known. If the soul has an existence then it should be known the way a pot, cloth etc. are known.
Resolving this doubt, the Guru says -
short: You believe in the existence of pot, cloth etc. because you have their knowledge.
But you do not believe in the existence of the knower of these objects.
What should one say about such knowledge?
(If the knower is absent, the knowledge is also absent. The presence of the knower is implicit in the knowledge of the objects.)

verses.title: Body and Soul Are not One
tr: Param buddhi krush dehma, sthool deh mati alp;
Deh hoy jo atama, ghate na aam vikalp.
iast: Parama buddhi kṛśa dehamāṁ, sthūḷa deha mati alpa;
Deha hoya jo ātamā, ghaṭe na āma vikalpa.
gu: પરમ બુદ્ધિ કૃશ દેહમાં, સ્થૂળ દેહ મતિ અલ્પ;
દેહ હોય જો આતમા, ઘટે ન આમ વિકલ્પ.
link: The attribute of knowing, is not of the body, it is of the soul which is separate from the body. This was the solution given by the Guru in verses 53 and 54.
Now in this verse 56, the same thing is established again through another logic (giving an example).
To uproot the disciple’s doubt completely that the body itself is the soul, and to strengthen his conviction, that the attribute of knowing is not the nature of the body; the Guru says -
words: If the body is the soul
Such a contradiction would not arise
short: Super intelligence is found in one who has a thin body.
While less intelligence is found in one who has a fat body.
If the body and the soul were one, such contradiction would not arise.
(This should not happen).

verses.title: Distinctness of Both Substances
tr: Jada chetanno bhinna chhe, keval pragat swabhav;
Ekpanu pamey nahi, trane kaal dvaybhav.
iast: Jaḍa cetanano bhinna che, kevaḷa pragaṭa svabhāva;
Ekapaṇuṁ pāme nahīṁ, traṇe kāḷa dvayabhāva.
gu: જડ ચેતનનો ભિન્ન છે, કેવળ પ્રગટ સ્વભાવ;
એકપણું પામે નહીં, ત્રણે કાળ દ્વયભાવ.
link: The soul is a substance with the attribute of knowingness and is separate from the body - after proving this through various logical arguments,
To further strengthen the true resolve of the disciple regarding the existence of the soul, in this concluding verse 57, the Guru says -
words: Lifeless (non-sentient, inanimate) and living (sentient, conscious) substance
short: The nature (characteristics) of the living beings (sentient) and the non-living beings (non-sentient) are always different.
Both have their own separate manifestation of characteristics which are entirely different.
The two separate substances cannot merge into one and
They remain as two separate substances at all times - past, present and the future (distinction between the two is unmistakably clear at all times.)

verses.title: Soul is Doubter of Itself!
tr: Atmani shanka karey, atma potey aap;
Shankano karnar te, acharaj eh amap.
iast: Ātmānī śaṁkā kare, ātmā pote āpa;
Śaṁkāno karanāra te, acaraja eha amāpa.
gu: આત્માની શંકા કરે, આત્મા પોતે આપ;
શંકાનો કરનાર તે, અચરજ એહ અમાપ.
link: From verse 49 - 57, the Guru satisfactorily resolves the disciple’s doubts, using profound arguments containing logic and examples.
Finally, expressing something astonishing that will lead the disciple into deep contemplation, the Guru says -
words: Beyond measure / immeasurable / cannot be measured
short: The existence of the soul is doubted by the soul itself.
It is a matter of immeasurable surprise that the soul doubts the existence of itself.
(It is a matter of surprise beyond measure that the soul is doubter of itself!)

verses.title: Disciple’s Conviction of Soul’s Existence
tr: Atmana astitvana, Aape kahya prakar;
Sambhav teno thay chhe, antar karye vichar.
iast: (2) Śaṁkā - śiṣya uvāca Ātmānā astitvanā, āpe kahyā prakāra;
Sambhava teno thāya che, aṁtara karye vicāra.
gu: (૨) શંકા - શિષ્ય ઉવાચ આત્માના અસ્તિત્વના, આપે કહ્યા પ્રકાર;
સમ્ભવ તેનો થાય છે, અંતર કર્યે વિચાર.
link: The disciple, eager to gain knowledge, put forth arguments regarding the existence of the soul, which the Guru resolved with counter arguments backed by logic and evidence.
By deeply contemplating upon the solution received from the Guru, the disciple is convinced about its correctness. He says -
words: Logic and examples explained by You
short: By internally contemplating over the clarification given by You, regarding the existence of the soul,
It seems possible.
(He declares that he has been clearly convinced by it and the existence of the soul is acceptable to him.)

verses.title: Doubt 1 - Soul is not Eternal
tr: Biji shanka thay tya, atma nahi avinash;
Dehyogthi upje, dehviyoge nash.
iast: Bījī śaṁkā thāya tyāṁ, ātmā nahi avināśa;
Dehayogathī ūpaje, dehaviyoge nāśa.
gu: બીજી શંકા થાય ત્યાં, આત્મા નહિ અવિનાશ;
દેહયોગથી ઊપજે, દેહવિયોગે નાશ.
link: After getting convinced of the truth of the first proposition (fundamental truth) i.e. the soul exists,
The disciple proceeds to his doubts about the second proposition i.e. the soul is eternal.
In this verse 60, under the influence of the Charvaka philosophy, from the perspective of gross modification, expressing the impermanence of the soul, the disciple says -
words: Takes birth with the union of the body
Gets destroyed on the separation with the body
short: Now arises the second doubt that the soul is not indestructible - immortal - eternal.
It is created with the association of the body and is destroyed with the separation from the body.
(The disciple feels that the soul might be arising with the formation of the body and might be destroyed at the time of death.)

verses.title: Doubt 2 - Soul is Momentary
tr: Athva vastu kshanik chhe, kshane kshane paltay;
E anubhavthi pan nahi, atma nitya janay.
iast: Athavā vastu kṣaṇika che, kṣaṇe kṣaṇe palaṭāya;
E anubhavathī paṇa nahīṁ, ātmā nitya jaṇāya.
gu: અથવા વસ્તુ ક્ષણિક છે, ક્ષણે ક્ષણે પલટાય;
એ અનુભવથી પણ નહીં, આત્મા નિત્ય જણાય.
link: Having expressed to the Guru - his doubt regarding the indestructible nature of the soul, that rose under the influence of the Charvaka philosophy, said that it seems the nature of the soul is creation and destruction.

Disciple now presents an argument that has arisen under the influence of the Buddhist philosophy from the perspective of subtle modification of life like the states of anger etc. that change every moment therefore it is momentary.
The disciple influenced by the Buddhist doctrine of momentariness, says -
words: (As it is seen) changing every moment
Soul is not known to be eternal
short: Or
Substance is seen to undergo modifications every moment (keeps on changing every moment) and therefore all objects are momentary.
Judging from experience too, the soul does not seem eternal.

verses.title: Reply 1 - Who Knows Creation and Destruction?
tr: Deh matra sanyog chhe, vali jad roopi drashya;
Chetanna utpatti laya, kona anubhav vashya?
iast: (2) Samādhāna - Sadguru uvāca Deha mātra saṁyoga che, vaḷī jaḍa rūpī dṛśya;
Cetananāṁ utpatti laya, konā anubhava vaśya?
gu: (૨) સમાધાન - સદ્ગુરુ ઉવાચ દેહ માત્ર સંયોગ છે, વળી જડ રૂપી દૃશ્ય;
ચેતનનાં ઉત્પત્તિ લય, કોના અનુભવ વશ્ય?
link: The Guru now provides a methodical - impactful - firm - wisdom- filled solution to the logical arguments arising due to the disciple's sequential thought process.
As a result of this, 'Soul is eternal' the second fundamental of samyagdarshan is proven to the disciple.
Establishing through different evidences like logic, experience and inference, the Guru completely uproots the doubt in the disciple's mind.
In verse 62 - 63, the Guru discusses whether there is any witness (knower) of the event of the soul's creation and destruction. The Guru says -
words: Body is formed by union of non-living matter
short: The body is formed by union of non-living matter and it is only in temporary association with the soul.
It is non-living, with form and visible.
Then who experiences i.e. who can have the knowledge of the creation and destruction of the soul. (As the body is without consciousness how and who knows that the soul is created and destroyed?)

verses.title: Knower Has to be Separate Entity
tr: Jena anubhav vashya e, utpann layanu jnan;
Te tethi juda vina, thay na keme bhan.
iast: Jenā anubhava vaśya e, utpanna layanuṁ jñāna;
Te tethī judā vinā, thāya na keme bhāna.
gu: જેના અનુભવ વશ્ય એ, ઉત્પન્ન લયનું જ્ઞાન;
તે તેથી જુદા વિના, થાય ન કેમે ભાન.
link: When contemplating upon the answer to the question posed in verse 62, there seems 2 possible options -  a) If it is said - that such experience depends on the body, then  it is not possible, as the body does not have the attribute of  knowingness - therefore cannot know the creation - destruction  of the soul.
In verse 62 itself the Guru negated the first option as the body is inanimate - has a form - is visible.

Now in verse 63, the Guru gives the solution to the second option -  b) Showing how the option that the creation and destruction of  the soul is known by consciousness is not possible, the Guru says -
words: Creation and destruction of the soul
Has to be separate from it
short: One who claims to know the birth and death of the soul must be different from it.
The knowledge of the emergence and extinction can in no way arise, unless the agency experiencing that knowledge is different from the object.

verses.title: Soul not Produced by Association
tr: Je sanyogo dekhiye, te te anubhav drashya;
Upje nahi sanyogathi, atma nitya pratyaksh.
iast: Je saṁyogo dekhiye, te te anubhava dṛśya;
Ūpaje nahi saṁyogathī, ātmā nitya pratyakṣa.
gu: જે સંયોગો દેખિયે, તે તે અનુભવ દૃશ્ય;
ઊપજે નહિ સંયોગથી, આત્મા નિત્ય પ્રત્યક્ષ.
link: In verse 62 - 63, the Guru proved that no one can know the creation and destruction of the soul. Therefore, the argument that the soul is created and destroyed through association with the body, is not backed by experience.
Now through logical reasoning in verses 64 - 66, the Guru will show that the soul is uncreated and indestructible.
Resolving the disciple’s probable doubt that the soul is also created (like the body) by some association the Guru says -
words: Soul is not born through any combination and for that reason
short: Whatever unions or combinations of atoms are observed and experienced (known) by the soul.
Reflecting on the nature of these combinations, we find none is competent to create a soul.
The soul is not observed to arise from the union of the elements of the body (combination of atoms).
Therefore (evidently) the soul is eternal and present at all times.

verses.title: Such Experience Cannot Exist
tr: Jadthi chetan upje, chetanthi jad thay;
Evo anubhav koine, kyare kadi na thay.
iast: Jaḍathī cetana ūpaje, cetanathī jaḍa thāya;
Evo anubhava koīne, kyāre kadī na thāya.
gu: જડથી ચેતન ઊપજે, ચેતનથી જડ થાય;
એવો અનુભવ કોઈને, ક્યારે કદી ન થાય.
link: The disciple’s belief is that it is probable that the soul is created from inanimate body. It lasts as long as the body lasts and is destroyed when separated from the body.
The three earlier verses (62 - 64) were the introduction to the solution of this argument.
Now addressing the argument directly in this verse 65, the Guru says -
short: No one has ever experienced.
Consciousness getting created from non-conscious matter.
And non-conscious matter getting created from consciousness.
(This experience has never been possible to anyone, anywhere, any time.)

verses.title: Soul is Definitely Eternal
tr: Koi sanyogothi nahi, jeni utpatti thay;
Nash na teno koima, tethi nitya saday.
iast: Koī saṁyogothī nahi, jenī utpatti thāya;
Nāśa na teno koīmāṁ, tethī nitya sadāya.
gu: કોઈ સંયોગોથી નહિ, જેની ઉત્પત્તિ થાય;
નાશ ન તેનો કોઈમાં, તેથી નિત્ય સદાય.
link: By contemplating upon every association, no such association is known from which the soul can be created. The soul is the knower of the association and not the product of any association.
Therefore, the Guru showed the fallacy of believing that the soul, which is not the product of association and is of the nature of knowingness, can be created from inanimate substance.
In verse 64 - 65, He established that the soul is uncreated. Now in this verse 66, the Guru establishes the soul’s indestructibility. He says -
words: Cannot be destroyed into anything else
short: That which cannot be created by any kind of union or combination of atoms or things,
Cannot be destroyed into anything else by the cessation of contact or disintegration of atoms.
According to the universal law one that is created can be destroyed; but the soul is not created so cannot be destroyed.
Therefore, it is eternal.
(Souls cannot be created by combination of objects or destroyed by separation of objects. Thus it is eternal.)

verses.title: Tendencies Confirm Soul’s Eternity
tr: Krodhadi tartamyata, sarpadikni mai;
Poorvajanma sanskar te, jiva nityata tyay.
iast: Krodhādi taratamyatā, sarpādikanī māṁya;
Pūrvajanma saṁskāra te, jīva nityatā tyāṁya.
gu: ક્રોધાદિ તરતમ્યતા, સર્પાદિકની માંય;
પૂર્વજન્મ સંસ્કાર તે, જીવ નિત્યતા ત્યાંય.
link: By deeply contemplating upon the Guru’s solution regarding the eternal nature of the soul, the disciple feels that his argument was baseless.

In this verse 67, to strengthen the faith of his, the Guru proves the eternal nature of the soul through inference. Giving an authentic evidence to prove the soul is not created and destroyed with the creation and destruction of the body, the Guru says -
words: Variation in tendencies of anger etc.
Due to the orientations of past lives
(This proves) for this reason also the soul is eternal
short: There is a burst of anger and other passions in snakes etc. from their very birth,
This is due to the tendencies acquired by them from previous births.
This proves the eternity of the soul.

verses.title: Reply 2 - Nature of Soul
tr: Atma dravye nitya chhe, paryaye paltay;
Baladi vay tranyanu, jnan ekne thay.
iast: Ātmā dravye nitya che, paryāye palaṭāya;
Bāḷādi vaya traṇyanuṁ, jñāna ekane thāya.
gu: આત્મા દ્રવ્યે નિત્ય છે, પર્યાયે પલટાય;
બાળાદિ વય ત્રણ્યનું, જ્ઞાન એકને થાય.
link: In verse 61, the disciple had raised the doubt that the object is seen to undergo modification every moment, therefore all objects are momentary.
Looking at the feelings of anger etc., which change every moment, the disciple feels that the soul is not eternal, rather it’s momentary.
Explaining the true nature of the soul, the Guru says -
words: But its states continue to change
Knowledge of all three stages are known by the same entity
short: The soul,
As a substance is eternal, unchanging.
But its states continue to change.
Childhood, adulthood, old age are different stages of life, but the eternal soul, which has the knowledge of all the three stages, is the same throughout.

verses.title: Narrator is not Momentary
tr: Athva jnan kshaniknu, je jani vadnar;
Vadnaro te kshanik nahi, kar anubhav nirdhar.
iast: Athavā jñāna kṣaṇikanuṁ, je jāṇī vadanāra;
Vadanāro te kṣaṇika nahi, kara anubhava nirdhāra.
gu: અથવા જ્ઞાન ક્ષણિકનું, જે જાણી વદનાર;
વદનારો તે ક્ષણિક નહિ, કર અનુભવ નિર્ધાર.
link: Although every substance has the qualities of permanence and impermanence, there are some who accept the existence of the soul, and yet believe that it is absolutely impermanent, created and destroyed every moment.
Logically proving the incorrectness of their belief, explaining how it is not possible for the soul to have momentary existence; the Guru says -
short: Or,
The narrator (speaker) who has the knowledge of momentary states, is not momentary himself.
(The speaker who knows and speaks about momentariness is not momentary, for the speaker must be continuous - to know and to speak.)
Ascertain this by your own experience (observation).

verses.title: No Substance is Completely Destroyed
tr: Kyare koi vastuno, keval hoy na nash;
Chetan pamey nash to, kema bhaley tapas.
iast: Kyāre koī vastuno, kevaḷa hoya na nāśa;
Cetana pāme nāśa to, kemāṁ bhaḷe tapāsa.
gu: ક્યારે કોઈ વસ્તુનો, કેવળ હોય ન નાશ;
ચેતન પામે નાશ તો, કેમાં ભળે તપાસ.
link: The Guru imparted a logical understanding to the disciple establishing the eternal nature of the soul, from verse 62 till this concluding verse 70.
Of all the rational solutions given by the Guru, this concluding verse is the pinnacle.
In this verse 70, drawing the disciple's attention to the universal law of conservation, accepted by science, applicable to every substance, the Guru skillfully proves that the soul is eternal.
Rebutting the false belief of the Buddhist philosophy of momentariness, and establishing the existence of the soul in all three periods of time, in this verse the Guru says -
words: Find in what it is transmuted / converted to
short: Never any substance can be entirely destroyed (into nothing).
Examine, if the soul is destroyed, what will it get converted into? (If consciousness is destroyed, find in what it is transmuted.)

tr: Karta jiva na karmano, karma j karta karma;
Athva sahaj swabhav ka, karma jivno dharma.
iast: (3) Śaṁkā - śiṣya uvāca Karttā jīva na karmano, karma ja karttā karma;
Athavā sahaja svabhāva kāṁ, karma jīvano dharma.
gu: (૩) શંકા - શિષ્ય ઉવાચ કર્ત્તા જીવ ન કર્મનો, કર્મ જ કર્ત્તા કર્મ;
અથવા સહજ સ્વભાવ કાં, કર્મ જીવનો ધર્મ.
link: The disciple presents arguments supporting his doubt, that has arisen under the influence of well-known philosophies and schools of thought, regarding the third fundamental, the doership of the soul.
In this first verse 71, the disciple says -
words: Bondage of karma is the nature of the soul
short: The soul is not the doer of karma, Karmas are done by karmas, hence karma is the doer of karma (present karmas are the result of past karmas). Or, karmas bind to the soul automatically (without any specific reason or condition). Or bondage of karma is the nature of the soul (so the soul can never be rid of karmas).

verses.title: Doubt 4, 5 - Matter or God is Doer
tr: Atma sada asang ne, karey prakruti bandh;
Athva Ishwar prerna, tethi jiva abandh.
iast: Ātmā sadā asaṁga ne, kare prakṛti baṁdha;
Athavā Īśvara preraṇā, tethī jīva abaṁdha.
gu: આત્મા સદા અસંગ ને, કરે પ્રકૃતિ બંધ;
અથવા ઈશ્વર પ્રેરણા, તેથી જીવ અબંધ.
link: Although existence and eternity of the soul is proved, the disciple is unable to grasp that the soul is the doer of karmas, so bent on proving that the soul is not the doer.
In the previous verse presented three arguments to support his view - now in this verse 72, presents two more.
It is clearly visible that both these arguments stem from the influence of Vedic philosophies (Sankhya, Nyaya etc.) which believe that the soul is unbound.
Caught in a whirlpool of doubts, yet having intense eagerness to know the truth, the disciple says -
words: Soul is always free and unattached
short: The soul is unattached and free so cannot be the creator of karma. Prakriti (matter) by its very nature creates bondage. Or it’s God who is the creator of souls and prompter of their karmas; all karmas are the result of His intervention and desire. Therefore, whether it’s prakriti (matter) or God, the soul cannot be held responsible for bondage of karmas.

verses.title: Concluding Contention
tr: Matey moksh upayno, koi na hetu janay;
Karmatanu kartapanu, ka nahi, ka nahi jaay.
iast: Māṭe mokṣa upāyano, koī na hetu jaṇāya;
Karmataṇuṁ kartāpaṇuṁ, kāṁ nahi, kāṁ nahi jāya.
gu: માટે મોક્ષ ઉપાયનો, કોઈ ન હેતુ જણાય;
કર્મતણું કર્તાપણું, કાં નહિ, કાં નહિ જાય.
link: Influenced by various beliefs prevalent in different philosophies regarding the non-doership of the soul, doubts have risen in the disciple regarding the soul as the doer of karmas.
In the two earlier verses (71 - 72), he put forth his arguments to show the soul cannot be the doer of karmas.
Expressing the conclusion, he is drawing based on what he has presented in the previous two verses, the disciple says -
words: Seems there is no reason / purpose
Or will never go / be eliminated
short: It seems, therefore, That there is no purpose in seeking the path of liberation. Either the soul is the non-doer of the karma. Or if the soul is the doer, it cannot be free from that doership nature; it stays forever.

verses.title: Reply 1 - Soul is Inspirer of Karma
tr: Hoy na chetan prerna, kaun grahe to karma?
Jadswabhav nahi prerna, juo vichari dharma.
iast: (3) Samādhāna - Sadguru uvāca Hoya na cetana preraṇā, koṇa grahe to karma?
Jaḍasvabhāva nahi preraṇā, juo vicārī dharma.
gu: (૩) સમાધાન - સદ્ગુરુ ઉવાચ હોય ન ચેતન પ્રેરણા, કોણ ગ્રહે તો કર્મ?
જડસ્વભાવ નહિ પ્રેરણા, જુઓ વિચારી ધર્મ.
link: In previous 3 verses (71 - 73), the disciple put forth to the Guru various options arising in his mind, regarding the soul not being the doer of karmas.
The Guru sequentially solves each of his arguments one by one in five verses (74 - 78).
In this verse, the Guru solves the argument of the first half of verse 71. The disciple says that the doer of the karma is karma itself. Resolving this argument, the Guru says -
words: Then who inspires / acquires the karmas
Has no capacity to inspire / acquire karmas
Ponder on the nature of substances
short: If the soul does not inspire the karma, who else will inspire it? Inanimate matter does not have the nature or capacity to inspire. Reflect upon the nature of both the substances - the sentient soul and non-sentient matter. It will be evident that conscious activity is not the nature of mundane matter or body. It's the soul which induces, thus it’s the doer of karmas.

verses.title: Reply 2, 3 - Soul’s Impure Tendency is Doer
tr: Jo chetan kartu nathi, nathi thata to karma;
Tethi sahaj swabhav nahi, tem j nahi jivdharma.
iast: Jo cetana karatuṁ nathī, nathī thatāṁ to karma;
Tethī sahaja svabhāva nahi, tema ja nahi jīvadharma.
gu: જો ચેતન કરતું નથી, નથી થતાં તો કર્મ;
તેથી સહજ સ્વભાવ નહિ, તેમ જ નહિ જીવધર્મ.
link: In the latter half of verse 71, the disciple said that karmas automatically get bound to the soul without any effort of the soul. Therefore, it is appropriate to believe that the soul is unbound.
If this is not the case and if the soul is the doer of karma, then to do karma becomes its inherent nature.
Clarifying both these options in this verse, the Guru says -
words: If soul activity does not exist
Then there would be no accumulation of karma
So karmas do not occur automatically
Nor is it the nature of the soul
short: The act of binding karmas takes place through the inspiration of consciousness. If the sentient soul does not engage in craving and aversion, karmas do not bind the soul. Therefore, neither does karma bind automatically nor it’s the innate nature of the soul. (Thus, the soul is the doer of karmas though not its nature, but it is its tendency which is contrary to its nature, and can be eliminated.)

verses.title: Reply 4 - Soul is not Absolutely Unbound
tr: Keval hota asang jo, bhasat taney na kem?
Asang chhe parmarthathi, pan nijbhane tem.
iast: Kevaḷa hota asaṁga jo, bhāsata tane na kema?
Asaṁga che paramārthathī, paṇa nijabhāne tema.
gu: કેવળ હોત અસંગ જો, ભાસત તને ન કેમ?
અસંગ છે પરમાર્થથી, પણ નિજભાને તેમ.
link: Two arguments that the disciple had put forth in verse 71 about the soul not being the doer of karma, were resolved perfectly by the Guru in verses 74 - 75.
Now the solution of the two options presented in verse 72 of the doctrine of doership of prakriti and doctrine of doership of God, will be given in verses 76 - 77.

In the first half of verse 72, the disciple said that the soul is non- attached and prakriti binds karma influenced by the Sankhya philosophy. The disciple projected the doership of karma on prakriti.
Explaining the flaw in the disciple’s reasoning and bringing about the right conviction, the Guru says -
words: If the soul is absolutely non-attached
Then why is it not experienced by you?
Soul is non-attached from higher viewpoint
But this can be attained when one experiences its pure Self
short: If the soul is absolutely non-attached and pure, if it is without the association of karma, Then why is it not experienced by you? You should have been able to experience it right from the beginning itself. It is non-attached from the absolute viewpoint, but from the relative viewpoint it becomes absolutely non-attached (liberated) only when it experiences the true nature, abides in it, and gets rid of all karmic bondage.

verses.title: Reply 5 - God is not Inspirer
tr: Karta Ishwar koi nahi, Ishwar shuddha swabhav;
Athva prerak te ganye, Ishwar doshprabhav.
iast: Kartā Īśvara koī nahi, Īśvara śuddha svabhāva;
Athavā preraka te gaṇye, Īśvara doṣaprabhāva.
gu: કર્તા ઈશ્વર કોઈ નહિ, ઈશ્વર શુદ્ધ સ્વભાવ;
અથવા પ્રેરક તે ગણ્યે, ઈશ્વર દોષપ્રભાવ.
link: In the latter half of verse 72, the disciple had said that God inspires the soul to do karma and therefore the soul is unbound.

That is, God has created the world and the activities of the world take place as per God’s will and inspiration. Whatever karmas are done by worldly beings are through God’s inspiration alone. Since there is no fault of the soul in doing karmas, the soul is proved unbound.
Resolving this argument of the disciple, the Guru says -
words: God is the achiever of purest state
Is considered the inspirer of karma of the soul
Then He would be deemed as flawed
short: There is no God who is the creator of universe or inspirer of actions of living beings. God is the soul who has achieved complete pure, natural state. If God is considered as inducing the souls to do actions (karmas). Then God will be associated with defects and contradictions.

verses.title: Soul is Doer
tr: Chetan jo nij bhanma, karta aap swabhav;
Varte nahi nij bhanma, karta karma-prabhav.
iast: Cetana jo nija bhānamāṁ, kartā āpa svabhāva;
Varte nahi nija bhānamāṁ, kartā karma-prabhāva.
gu: ચેતન જો નિજ ભાનમાં, કર્તા આપ સ્વભાવ;
વર્તે નહિ નિજ ભાનમાં, કર્તા કર્મ-પ્રભાવ.
link: In verses 74 - 77, the Guru perfectly explained how the soul is the doer of karma, through simple and heart-touching logical arguments.
Out of selfless compassion, the Guru guides the disciple’s flow of thoughts which have been blemished by one-sidedness, in the right direction and in conclusion expounds the eternal principle.
In verse 73, the disciple expressed that there seems to be no purpose in pursuing the means of liberation. Clearing the disciple’s confusion the Guru says -
words: If the soul is aware of its true nature
It’s the doer of its pure nature
If it is not in the awareness of its true nature
It becomes the doer of karmas
short: If the soul abides in the awareness of its pure nature (i.e. when it becomes steadfast in its flawless, non-attached nature), Then it becomes the doer of its pure nature (in the sense of its manifestation). When it does not abide in the awareness of its pure nature, Then, it is the doer of impure feelings which are instrumental in binding material karmas.

verses.title: Doubt 1 - Karma Devoid of Knowingness
tr: Jiva karma karta kaho, pan bhokta nahi soy;
Shu samje jada karma ke, fal parinami hoy?
iast: (4) Śaṁkā - śiṣya uvāca Jīva karma kartā kaho, paṇa bhoktā nahi soya;
Śuṁ samaje jaḍa karma ke, phaḷa pariṇāmī hoya?
gu: (૪) શંકા - શિષ્ય ઉવાચ જીવ કર્મ કર્તા કહો, પણ ભોક્તા નહિ સોય;
શું સમજે જડ કર્મ કે, ફળ પરિણામી હોય?
link: To show that it is impossible for the soul to be the receiver of the fruits of karma, the disciple presents his first argument -
words: Can be accepted / you may say
Lifeless karma know 9) Fal parinami hoy = That they should inflict the fruits of karmas upon the doer (giving result - parinami)
short: It can be accepted that the soul is the doer of karma, but it does not necessarily follow that it is the receiver (enjoyer or sufferer) of karmas, as
How can inanimate (lifeless matter) karma have the understanding to give fruits of the karmas to the doer, the soul (in a particular way at a particular time).

verses.title: Doubt 2 - God Bestows Fruits of Karma
tr: Faldata Ishwar ganye, bhoktapanu sadhay;
Em kahye Ishwartanu, Ishwarpanu j jaay.
iast: Phaḷadātā Īśvara gaṇye, bhoktāpaṇuṁ sadhāya;
Ema kahye Īśvarataṇuṁ, Īśvarapaṇuṁ ja jāya.
gu: ફળદાતા ઈશ્વર ગણ્યે, ભોક્તાપણું સધાય;
એમ કહ્યે ઈશ્વરતણું, ઈશ્વરપણું જ જાય.
link: As the thinking of the disciple progresses, he reasons that karmas are devoid of the ability to know, therefore cannot give the fruits of karmas on their own.
Hence one must believe in the inspiration of some conscious entity, which can be none other than God.
However, stating the difficulty which arises in harbouring this belief, the disciple says -
words: The giver of fruits of karmas
If you take God to be
Then the soul being the receiver
short: If God is accepted as the bestower (giver) of the fruits of karmas, then it can be established that the soul is the receiver of the fruits of karmas.
However, if this is accepted, God will lose the state of Godhood. (If God is accepted as the fruit-giver then Godliness cannot be associated with Him.)

verses.title: Fallacious Conclusion
tr: Ishwar siddha thaya vina, jagat niyam nahi hoy;
Pachhi shubhashubh karmana, bhogyasthan nahi koy.
iast: Īśvara siddha thayā vinā, jagata niyama nahi hoya;
Pachī śubhāśubha karmanāṁ, bhogyasthāna nahi koya.
gu: ઈશ્વર સિદ્ધ થયા વિના, જગત નિયમ નહિ હોય;
પછી શુભાશુભ કર્મનાં, ભોગ્યસ્થાન નહિ કોય.
link: While deeply contemplating over whether the soul can be considered the receiver of the fruits of karmas or not, the disciple has understood that God cannot be proved to be the bestower of the fruits of karmas in any manner.
However, if it is not God, then many other difficulties arise. Expressing his confusion, he says -
words: For the fruition of good - bad karmas
short: Without establishing the existence of God as the power that maintains order and system in the world; there will be anarchy and chaos everywhere.
There will also be no designated places like heaven and hell to obtain the results of good and bad karmas.
(Under such circumstances one has to admit that the soul cannot be the receiver of the fruits of karmas.)

verses.title: Reply 1 - Process of Bondage
tr: Bhaavkarma nij kalpana, matey chetanroop;
Jivaviryani sfurana, grahan karey jadadhoop.
iast: (4) Samādhāna - Sadguru uvāca Bhāvakarma nija kalpanā, māṭe cetanarūpa;
Jīvavīryanī sphuraṇā, grahaṇa kare jaḍadhūpa.
gu: (૪) સમાધાન - સદ્ગુરુ ઉવાચ ભાવકર્મ નિજ કલ્પના, માટે ચેતનરૂપ;
જીવવીર્યની સ્ફુરણા, ગ્રહણ કરે જડધૂપ.
