link: In the following 5 verses - the Guru takes up sequentially the points raised by the disciple regarding ‘soul is the receiver of fruits of karmas’ and puts his doubts at rest.

In verse 79, the disciple had said that, how can inanimate karma have the understanding to give fruits. Karma lacking consciousness is incapable of giving fruits and therefore the soul is not the receiver of the fruits of karma.
The Guru resolves this doubt in 3 verses (82 - 84).
To explain how the soul is the receiver, the Guru first shows why and how the association with karma takes place. He says -
short: The soul’s impure feelings like impulses, desires originate within the soul and they are therefore conscious or sentient acts.
They induce the soul’s energy to work in attracting the karmic particles, resulting in its bondage with the soul.
(The passions of the soul are the cause of bondage of karmic matter to it.)

verses.title: Non-Sentient Matter Shows Effects
tr: Jher sudha samje nahin, jiva khay fal thay;
Em shubhashubh karmanu, bhoktapanu janay.
iast: Jhera sudhā samaje nahīṁ, jīva khāya phaḷa thāya;
Ema śubhāśubha karmanuṁ, bhoktāpaṇuṁ jaṇāya.
gu: ઝેર સુધા સમજે નહીં, જીવ ખાય ફળ થાય;
એમ શુભાશુભ કર્મનું, ભોક્તાપણું જણાય.
link: From verse 82, the Guru is explaining how the material karmas bound by the soul give fruits and how the soul receives them.
Using an example that will make it easy to understand how inanimate karma gives fruits, the Guru says -
words: So with regards to good or bad karmas
Understand the enjoyment to be in the soul
short: Poison and nectar do not know their qualities or effects but the person who consumes them experiences its results.
In the same way, the fruition of auspicious and inauspicious karmas are experienced by the soul. (Similarly the soul bears the consequences of good and bad karmas.)

verses.title: Nothing Happens Without Reason
tr: Ek raank ne ek nrup, e adi je bhed;
Karan vina na karya te, te j shubhashubh vedya.
iast: Eka rāṇka ne eka nṛpa, e ādi je bheda;
Kāraṇa vinā na kārya te, te ja śubhāśubha vedya.
gu: એક રાણ્ક ને એક નૃપ, એ આદિ જે ભેદ;
કારણ વિના ન કાર્ય તે, તે જ શુભાશુભ વેદ્ય.
link: In verses 82 - 83, the Guru explained the process of karmic bondage and proved that accumulated karmas give fruits on their own at the appropriate time.
Proving that the soul is the receiver of the fruits of auspicious and inauspicious karma through a familiar example, the Guru says -
words: Without cause there is no effect
Likewise the result of good and bad karmas are experienced
short: One person is a pauper and another is a prince, and similar differences are observed in the world.
Know likewise the results of good and bad karmas are experienced because never anything happens without a reason.
(Such differences prove that there is fruition of auspicious and inauspicious karmas of the past; as effect is not possible without a cause.)

verses.title: Reply 2 - Karma Fructify by Their Own Nature
tr: Faldata Ishwartani, ema nathi jaroor;
Karma swabhave pariname, thay bhogthi dur.
iast: Phaḷadātā Īśvarataṇī, emāṁ nathī jarūra;
Karma svabhāve pariṇame, thāya bhogathī dūra.
gu: ફળદાતા ઈશ્વરતણી, એમાં નથી જરૂર;
કર્મ સ્વભાવે પરિણમે, થાય ભોગથી દૂર.
link: In verse 80, the disciple had said that if God is considered to be the bestower of the fruits of karmas, then it can be established that the soul is the receiver of the fruits of karma. However, if that is accepted, then His Godliness itself does not remain.
The disciple’s mind was confused between these two options and unable to arrive at the right conclusion. To eliminate this confusion of the disciple, in this verse, the Guru says -
words: Karmas fruitify by their own nature
And exhausted as soon as their effects are experienced
short: There is no necessity to consider God as fruit-giver, imparting the results of the past karmas.
Karmas fruitify by their own nature and they shed away after giving their fruits; as soon as their effects are experienced.

verses.title: Deep Subject Explained Briefly
tr: Te te bhogya visheshna, sthanak dravya swabhav;
Gahan vaat chhe shishya aa, kahi sankshepe saav.
iast: Te te bhogya viśeṣanāṁ, sthānaka dravya svabhāva;
Gahana vāta che śiṣya ā, kahī saṁkṣepe sāva.
gu: તે તે ભોગ્ય વિશેષનાં, સ્થાનક દ્રવ્ય સ્વભાવ;
ગહન વાત છે શિષ્ય આ, કહી સંક્ષેપે સાવ.
link: In verse 81, the disciple had said that without establishing the existence of God, no law will prevail in the world; then there will be no designated places like heaven and hell to obtain the fruits of one’s deeds.
If God is established as the fruit-giver and the creator of the world then it hinders His Godliness.
Solving this confusion of the disciple - the Guru says -
words: Experiences the fruits of its karmas
Due to self-nature of the substances
The subject matter is very deep
short: In order that the soul experiences the fruits of karma, in the form of enjoyment and sufferings, there are associated places and forms, through their inherent Self-nature.
Oh disciple! This is a deep topic, but it has been stated very briefly, over here.
(The philosophy of heaven and hell are described in detail in scriptures, but being difficult to grasp, only a brief idea is given here.)

verses.title: Doubt 1 - There Cannot be Liberation
tr: Karta bhokta jiva ho, pan teno nahi moksh;
Vityo kaal anant pan, vartaman chhe dosh.
iast: (5) Śaṁkā - śiṣya uvāca Kartā bhoktā jīva ho, paṇa teno nahi mokṣa;
Vītyo kāḷa anaṁta paṇa, vartamāna che doṣa.
gu: (૫) શંકા - શિષ્ય ઉવાચ કર્તા ભોક્તા જીવ હો, પણ તેનો નહિ મોક્ષ;
વીત્યો કાળ અનંત પણ, વર્તમાન છે દોષ.
link: In the first verse, presenting an argument in support of his doubt regarding the fifth fundamental truth - 'There is liberation.'
Which has arisen under the influence of Purva Mimansa philosophy, the disciple says -
words: There is no liberation from it
short: Though, the soul may be the acquirer and bearer of consequences,
But it cannot achieve liberation from them (absolute freedom from bondage is not possible because),
Infinite time has passed and yet the impurity still continues to prevail.
(If liberation was possible then despite infinite time having passed by, why has the soul not attained liberation till date.)

verses.title: Doubt 2 - Soul is Nowhere Without Karma
tr: Shubh karey fal bhogve, devadi gatimai;
Ashubh karey narkadi fal, karma rahit na kyai.
iast: Śubha kare phaḷa bhogave, devādi gati māṁya;
Aśubha kare narakādi phaḷa, karma rahita na kyāṁya.
gu: શુભ કરે ફળ ભોગવે, દેવાદિ ગતિ માંય;
અશુભ કરે નરકાદિ ફળ, કર્મ રહિત ન ક્યાંય.
link: The disciple’s understanding has grown and his discriminating intellect has bloomed.
Looking at the transmigration of worldly souls in the four states of existence, another logical argument supporting his doubt regarding the liberation of the soul arises in him.
Presenting it to the Guru, he says -
words: Bears the fruits in hell etc.
short: If the soul does auspicious karmas, it enjoys its fruits in the state of heavenly beings etc.
If it does inauspicious karmas, it suffers its fruits in hell etc.
The soul is nowhere without karmas.
[Never / nowhere is the soul found without karmas in any state of existence (gati).]

verses.title: Reply 1 - Cessation of Karma is Liberation
tr: Jem shubhashubh karmapada, janya safal praman;
Tem nivrutti safalta, matey moksh sujaan.
iast: (5) Samādhāna - Sadguru uvāca Jema śubhāśubha karmapada, jāṇyāṁ saphaḷa pramāṇa;
Tema nivṛtti saphaḷatā, māṭe mokṣa sujāṇa.
gu: (૫) સમાધાન - સદ્ગુરુ ઉવાચ જેમ શુભાશુભ કર્મપદ, જાણ્યાં સફળ પ્રમાણ;
તેમ નિવૃત્તિ સફળતા, માટે મોક્ષ સુજાણ.
link: In verse 87, the disciple had expressed a doubt that if liberation of the soul was possible, then despite infinite time having passed by, why has it not attained liberation till date?
The Guru has given the solution to this doubt in two verses (89 - 90).

In this verse (89), the Guru proves the existence of liberation and in  the next verse (90) the Guru explains why liberation has not been attained and what should be done to attain it. The Guru says -
words: Just as good and bad karmas
Similarly the cessation of karmas is also fruitful
short: Just as good and bad karmas are fruitful in their way, cessation of karmas is also fruitful.
O wise one, there is therefore liberation.

verses.title: Elimination of Impure Feelings
tr: Vityo kaal anant te, karma shubhashubh bhaav;
Teh shubhashubh chhedta, upje moksh swabhav.
iast: Vītyo kāḷa anaṁta te, karma śubhāśubha bhāva;
Teha śubhāśubha chedatāṁ, ūpaje mokṣa svabhāva.
gu: વીત્યો કાળ અનંત તે, કર્મ શુભાશુભ ભાવ;
તેહ શુભાશુભ છેદતાં, ઊપજે મોક્ષ સ્વભાવ.
link: Explaining what is the cause of the soul’s transmigration and how an end can be brought to that, the Guru says -
words: Arises liberation which is the nature of the soul
short: Since infinite time, the soul is engaged in auspicious and inauspicious feelings.
With the snapping / breaking / destroying of it the soul attains liberation which is its true nature.

verses.title: Reply 2 - Concept of Liberation
tr: Dehadik sanyogno, atyantik viyog;
Siddha moksh shashwat padey, nij anant sukhbhog.
iast: Dehādika saṁyogano, ātyaṁtika viyoga;
Siddha mokṣa śāśvata pade, nija anaṁta sukhabhoga.
gu: દેહાદિક સંયોગનો, આત્યંતિક વિયોગ;
સિદ્ધ મોક્ષ શાશ્વત પદે, નિજ અનંત સુખભોગ.
link: In verse 88, the disciple had said that if the soul does auspicious karmas it goes to heaven etc. and if it does inauspicious karmas it goes to hell etc. However, the soul is not without karmas at any place.
The disciple is unable to find any such place where the soul has no  association of karma.
Resolving this doubt and describing the nature of liberation, the Guru says -
words: Where it enjoys its own bliss
short: With the permanent disassociation of the soul from the body and other associations (like karmas),
It eternally stays in the liberated state.
And experiences its own infinite bliss.

verses.title: Doubt 1 - Annihilating Karma in One Lifetime
tr: Hoy kadapi mokshpada, nahi avirodh upay;
Karmo kaal anantna, shathi chhedya jaay?
iast: (6) Śaṁkā - śiṣya uvāca Hoya kadāpi mokṣapada, nahi avirodha upāya;
Karmo kāḷa anaṁtanāṁ, śāthī chedyāṁ jāya?
gu: (૬) શંકા - શિષ્ય ઉવાચ હોય કદાપિ મોક્ષપદ, નહિ અવિરોધ ઉપાય;
કર્મો કાળ અનંતનાં, શાથી છેદ્યાં જાય?
link: After attaining the correct understanding of the nature of liberation and its benefits, the disciple desirous of putting an end to his transmigration, is eager to know the correct method to attain liberation.
He has some doubts regarding the path of liberation. Presenting his confusion, the disciple says -
short: Even if there is a state of liberation, there appears no undisputed path to attain it.
How can karmas accumulated since infinite times, be annihilated in this short lifespan?

verses.title: Doubt 2 - No Undisputed Means to Liberation
tr: Athva mat darshan ghana, kahey upay anek;
Tema mat sacho kayo, baney na eh vivek.
iast: Athavā mata darśana ghaṇāṁ, kahe upāya aneka;
Temāṁ mata sāco kayo, bane na eha viveka.
gu: અથવા મત દર્શન ઘણાં, કહે ઉપાય અનેક;
તેમાં મત સાચો કયો, બને ન એહ વિવેક.
link: The disciple presented an argument supporting his doubt that there are no undisputed means, that is, no authentic unfailing path to attain liberation.
Putting forth a second argument in support of the same doubt, he says -
words: There are many views and schools of thought
Stipulate the path in numerous ways
short: Or
There are many opinions and philosophies which show innumerable ways of liberation and claim its infallibility and superiority.
It is difficult to decide as to which of the proposed path is correct and worthy of adoption by a true seeker.

verses.title: Doubt 3 - Multiplicity of Views Regarding Caste and Clothing
tr: Kai jatima moksh chhe, kaya veshma moksh;
Eno nishchay na baney, ghana bhed e dosh.
iast: Kaī jātimāṁ mokṣa che, kayā veṣamāṁ mokṣa;
Eno niścaya nā bane, ghaṇā bheda e doṣa.
gu: કઈ જાતિમાં મોક્ષ છે, કયા વેષમાં મોક્ષ;
એનો નિશ્ચય ના બને, ઘણા ભેદ એ દોષ.
link: The thoughtful disciple has studied several religions, philosophies and is aware of their beliefs. He is confused by the differences in the path of liberation propounded by them and therefore feels there is no undisputed path of liberation.
Putting forth the third argument in support of his doubt, he says -
short: Which caste or clothes are required to attain liberation? Because of the diverse opinions, it is extremely difficult to determine the undisputed path of liberation.

verses.title: Conclusion Drawn From Discussion
tr: Tethi em janay chhe, maley na moksh upay;
Jivadi janya tano, sho upkar j thay?
iast: Tethī ema jaṇāya che, maḷe na mokṣa upāya;
Jīvādi jāṇyā taṇo, śo upakāra ja thāya?
gu: તેથી એમ જણાય છે, મળે ન મોક્ષ ઉપાય;
જીવાદિ જાણ્યા તણો, શો ઉપકાર જ થાય?
link: The disciple presented 3 arguments (verses 92 - 94) regarding the last fundamental - ‘There is a path of liberation.’
Expressing the conclusion he has drawn regarding the path of liberation on account of his doubt, he says -
short: Therefore, it seems that the path of liberation is not obtainable.
Then what benefit can be gained, by knowing about the soul etc.?

verses.title: Intense Longing for Path
tr: Panche uttarthi thayu, samadhan sarvang;
Samju moksh upay to, uday uday sadbhagya.
iast: Pāṁce uttarathī thayuṁ, samādhāna sarvāṁga;
Samajuṁ mokṣa upāya to, udaya udaya sadbhāgya.
gu: પાંચે ઉત્તરથી થયું, સમાધાન સર્વાંગ;
સમજું મોક્ષ ઉપાય તો, ઉદય ઉદય સદ્ભાગ્ય.
link: In verses 92 - 94, the disciple put forth 3 arguments supporting his doubt regarding the path of liberation.
In verse 95, he expressed the importance of understanding the undisputed path of liberation.
Now, in the concluding verse, exhibiting an intense longing to understand the path of liberation, he says -
words: If I understand the means of liberation
short: Upon receiving the answers to my earlier five questions,
I am entirely satisfied as all my doubts have been cleared.
I will consider myself the most fortunate one if I would get similar satisfaction regarding the path of liberation.

verses.title: Assurance to Disciple
tr: Panche uttarni thai, atma vishe pratit;
Thashe mokshopayani, sahaj pratit e reet.
iast: (6) Samādhāna - Sadguru uvāca Pāṁce uttaranī thaī, ātmā viṣe pratīta;
Thāśe mokṣopāyanī, sahaja pratīta e rīta.
gu: (૬) સમાધાન - સદ્ગુરુ ઉવાચ પાંચે ઉત્તરની થઈ, આત્મા વિષે પ્રતીત;
થાશે મોક્ષોપાયની, સહજ પ્રતીત એ રીત.
link: The solutions given by the Guru have kindled the disciple's eagerness to know the path of liberation as, without knowing it all other knowledge is useless, so it is extremely important to understand it.
The Guru too, reciprocates to the disciple’s feelings with an equally befitting response. The Guru gives a detailed solution regarding it in 22 verses.
Before beginning to resolve the disciple’s arguments sequentially, assuring him, the Guru says -
words: Belief in the soul has arisen
Will arise in the means of liberation
short: Just as you are convinced in the existence etc. of the soul through the five replies,
In the same way, you will also be convinced easily, about the means of liberation.

tr: Karmabhaav ajnan chhe, mokshbhaav nijvas;
Andhkar ajnan sama, nashe jnanprakash.
iast: Karmabhāva ajñāna che, mokṣabhāva nijavāsa;
Aṁdhakāra ajñāna sama, nāśe jñānaprakāśa.
gu: કર્મભાવ અજ્ઞાન છે, મોક્ષભાવ નિજવાસ;
અંધકાર અજ્ઞાન સમ, નાશે જ્ઞાનપ્રકાશ.
link: In verse 92 the disciple had posed the argument that, even if the state of liberation exists, no undisputed path to attain it seems to be known. Moreover, how can karmas that have been accumulated since infinite times be annihilated in this short lifespan?
The Guru has answered this argument from verses 98 - 104 (98 - 101 = first line, 102 - 104 = second line).
In the opening verse of the solution to the doubt regarding the undisputed means of liberation, the Guru says -
words: Impurity of the soul arising due to karmas
short: Impurity of the soul is ignorance of the Self.
While abiding in the Self is liberation.
Just as darkness gets destroyed by light, ignorance gets destroyed by light of knowledge of the Self.

verses.title: Path of Bondage and Liberation
tr: Je je karan bandhna, teh bandhno panth;
Te karan chhedak dasha, mokshpanth bhavant.
iast: Je je kāraṇa baṁdhanāṁ, teha baṁdhano paṁtha;
Te kāraṇa chedaka daśā, mokṣapaṁtha bhavaaṁta.
gu: જે જે કારણ બંધનાં, તેહ બંધનો પંથ;
તે કારણ છેદક દશા, મોક્ષપંથ ભવઅંત.
link: Expanding on the truth stated earlier, now the Guru will throw light on the subtleties of the path of liberation.
In verse 99, the first of the three verses explaining the right method of liberation, the Guru says -
short: Whatever are the causes of bondage is the path of bondage.
The state that eliminates them is the path of liberation.
And is the end of cycles of birth and death.

verses.title: Path of Liberation - Negative Assertion
tr: Raag, dwesh, ajnan e, mukhya karmani granth;
Thay nivrutti jehathi, te j mokshno panth.
iast: Rāga, dveṣa, ajñāna e, mukhya karmanī graṁtha;
Thāya nivṛtti jehathī, te ja mokṣano paṁtha.
gu: રાગ, દ્વેષ, અજ્ઞાન એ, મુખ્ય કર્મની ગ્રંથ;
થાય નિવૃત્તિ જેહથી, તે જ મોક્ષનો પંથ.
link: Showing the causes resorting to which one advances on the path of bondage, and the causes retiring from which one advances on the path of liberation, the Guru now says -
short: Attachment, aversion and ignorance are the main knots of karma.
That by which one recedes from them constitutes the path of liberation.

verses.title: Path of Liberation - Positive Assertion
tr: Atma sat chaitanyamay, sarvabhaas rahit;
Jethi keval pamiye, mokshpanth te reet.
iast: Ātmā sat caitanyamaya, sarvābhāsa rahita;
Jethī kevaḷa pāmiye, mokṣapaṁtha te rīta.
gu: આત્મા સત્ ચૈતન્યમય, સર્વાભાસ રહિત;
જેથી કેવળ પામિયે, મોક્ષપંથ તે રીત.
link: In verse 100, the Guru said that one’s progress on the path of liberation is proportional to the extent that he has reduced likes, dislikes, ignorance.
Thus in verse 100, the Guru explained the path of liberation through a method of negative assertion and in verse 101, explains through a method of positive assertion.
Illuminating characteristic of the path of liberation as abidance in the pure Self, the Guru says -
short: The nature of the soul is eternal existence, consciousness, devoid of all illusions.
The way by which one experiences and abides in the pure Self is the path of liberation.

verses.title: Chief Karma is Deluding Karma
tr: Karma anant prakarna, tema mukhye aath;
Tema mukhye mohaniya, hanay te kahu paath.
iast: Karma anaṁta prakāranāṁ, temāṁ mukhye āṭha;
Temāṁ mukhye mohanīya, haṇāya te kahuṁ pāṭha.
gu: કર્મ અનંત પ્રકારનાં, તેમાં મુખ્યે આઠ;
તેમાં મુખ્યે મોહનીય, હણાય તે કહું પાઠ.
link: In verses 100 - 101, an extremely important essence was expanded. One’s progress on the path of liberation is proportional to the extent that he has reduced likes, dislikes, ignorance and gained abidance in the Self.
Until now, the Guru explained the path of liberation from the perspective of eliminating impure feelings.

Now in 3 verses (102 - 104) He answers the argument expressed by the disciple in the latter half of verse 92 that karmas have been accumulated since infinite times, how can they be annihilated in a short lifespan?
In this verse, explaining from the perspective of annihilating material karmas, the Guru says -
words: Of which eight are main ones
Amongst them, chief is deluding karma
To destroy them / for its destruction
I will speak / state the lesson
short: There are infinite types of karmas.
Of these, there are mainly eight broad divisions.
Amongst these eight, deluding karma is the most prominent.
I will show the way to destroy it.

verses.title: Unfailing Remedy to Destroy Deluding Karma
tr: Karma mohaniya bhed bey, darshan charitra naam;
Haney bodh vitragta, achuk upay aam.
iast: Karma mohanīya bheda be, darśana cāritra nāma;
Haṇe bodha vītarāgatā, acūka upāya āma.
gu: કર્મ મોહનીય ભેદ બે, દર્શન ચારિત્ર નામ;
હણે બોધ વીતરાગતા, અચૂક ઉપાય આમ.
link: Deluding karma is instrumental in binding of all the other karmas. Therefore it is extremely essential to know the means to destroy it to attain liberation, which is the annihilation of all karmas.
Revealing the unfailing means to destroy deluding karma, in this verse the Guru says -
short: The deluding karmas are of two types pertaining to belief and behaviour, namely faith deluding karma and conduct deluding karma.
They can be destroyed by enlightenment and dispassion.
That is the unfailing remedy.

verses.title: Evident Experience of All
tr: Karmabandh krodhadithi, haney kshamadik teh;
Pratyaksh anubhav sarvane, ema sho sandeh?
iast: Karmabaṁdha krodhādithī, haṇe kṣamādika teha;
Pratyakṣa anubhava sarvane, emāṁ śo saṁdeha?
gu: કર્મબંધ ક્રોધાદિથી, હણે ક્ષમાદિક તેહ;
પ્રત્યક્ષ અનુભવ સર્વને, એમાં શો સંદેહ?
link: The Guru made it crystal clear in the earlier verses that the path by which deluding karma is annihilated is the path of liberation.
Now in this verse, He explains what one should do at the practical level to attain liberation. The truth has been explained through an example, making it palatable even to a layman.
Ensuring a doubtless resolve regarding the path of liberation, the Guru says -
words: What doubt can be there in this?
short: The bondage of karma due to anger etc. can be destroyed by forgiveness etc.
That is the evident experience of everyone.
How can there be any doubt about it?

verses.title: Reply 2 - Impartial Perspective Leads to Liberation
tr: Chhodi mat darshan tano, agrah tem vikalp;
Kahyo marg aa sadhashe, janma tehna alp.
iast: Choḍī mata darśana taṇo, āgraha tema vikalpa;
Kahyo mārga ā sādhaśe, janma tehanā alpa.
gu: છોડી મત દર્શન તણો, આગ્રહ તેમ વિકલ્પ;
કહ્યો માર્ગ આ સાધશે, જન્મ તેહના અલ્પ.
link: In verse 93, the disciple had said that there are many sects and schools of thought prevalent in the world, which expound different paths to attain liberation, and it is not possible to determine which of those is correct.
Having studied the beliefs of various religions and philosophies, the disciple is confused.
Putting an end to his confusion, the Guru says -
words: The path of liberation indicated here
short: Giving up strong insistence and choices about his beliefs and philosophies,
One who pursues the above mentioned path,
Shall attain liberation in only a few births.

verses.title: Complete Understanding of Six Aphorisms
tr: Shatpadna shatprashna te, poochhya kari vichar;
Te padni sarvangata, mokshmarg nirdhar.
iast: Ṣaṭpadanāṁ ṣaṭpraśna teṁ, pūchyāṁ karī vicāra;
Te padanī sarvāṁgatā, mokṣamārga nirdhāra.
gu: ષટ્પદનાં ષટ્પ્રશ્ન તેં, પૂછ્યાં કરી વિચાર;
તે પદની સર્વાંગતા, મોક્ષમાર્ગ નિર્ધાર.
link: Having asked the questions with a genuine desire to know the truth, the worthy disciple receives the apt solutions from the Guru.
Strengthening the conviction in the path of liberation, the Guru says -
words: Determine it as the sure path of liberation
short: You have very thoughtfully asked six questions regarding the six fundamental truths.
Determine with certainty that a complete understanding of these fundamental truths from multiple viewpoints is the sure path of liberation.

verses.title: Reply 3 - Caste or Clothing Have No Role
tr: Jati, veshno bhed nahi, kahyo marg jo hoy;
Sadhe te mukti lahey, ema bhed na koy.
iast: Jāti, veṣano bheda nahi, kahyo mārga jo hoya;
Sādhe te mukti lahe, emāṁ bheda na koya.
gu: જાતિ, વેષનો ભેદ નહિ, કહ્યો માર્ગ જો હોય;
સાધે તે મુક્તિ લહે, એમાં ભેદ ન કોય.
link: The Guru illuminated the right path of liberation to the worthy disciple.
Now resolving his last question regarding the path of liberation, expressed in verse 94, that which caste (or gender) and attire is required to attain liberation, the Guru says -
words: Said path / prescribed path of liberation
short: There is no discrimination of caste or garb (attire) in the prescribed path of liberation.
Whoever pursues it, attains liberation;
There is no doubt in this.

verses.title: Four Virtues of Aspirant
tr: Kashayni upshantata, matra mokshabhilash;
Bhavey khed antar daya, te kahie jignas.
iast: Kaṣāyanī upaśāṁtatā, mātra mokṣaabhilāṣa;
Bhave kheda aṁtara dayā, te kahīe jijñāsa.
gu: કષાયની ઉપશાંતતા, માત્ર મોક્ષઅભિલાષ;
ભવે ખેદ અંતર દયા, તે કહીએ જિજ્ઞાસ.
link: Having established the path of liberation in the earlier verses (97 - 107), now a complete stepwise course for the pursuit of liberation has been described in 6 verses (second group).
The ascending sequence of the stages of spiritual development (gunasthanak) has been subtly woven into it.

In this verse 108, showing who is worthy of attaining the path of supreme truth, what virtues should have developed in him, so that he can be called an aspirant of the path of liberation, the Guru says -
short: One whose passions have subsided, only desire is for liberation, who has grief for cycles of birth and death, who holds compassion for all from within is called an aspirant for liberation.

verses.title: Guru’s Guidance Triggers Inner Quest
tr: Te jignasu jivne, thay Sadgurubodh;
To pamey samkitne, varte antarshodh.
iast: Te jijñāsu jīvane, thāya Sadgurubodha;
To pāme samakitane, varte aṁtaraśodha.
gu: તે જિજ્ઞાસુ જીવને, થાય સદ્ગુરુબોધ;
તો પામે સમકિતને, વર્તે અંતરશોધ.
link: Having perfectly shown the attributes by which an aspirant who is truly worthy of the path to liberation can be recognised.
Now, the Guru describes how the one with such a state advances sequentially on the path, after the association with a Sadguru. He says -
words: If such a truth seeker / aspirant soul
Gets advice from a true Guru
Leads a life of internal purification
short: If such a spiritual aspirant gets guidance from a true Guru,
He attains unwavering faith in Him and His teachings. He then engages in an inner quest and embarks on the journey of self-purification.

verses.title: Achieves Pure Experiential Faith
tr: Mat darshan agrah taji, varte Sadgurulaksh;
Lahey shuddh samkit te, jema bhed na paksh.
iast: Mata darśana āgraha tajī, varte Sadgurulakṣa;
Lahe śuddha samakita te, jemāṁ bheda na pakṣa.
gu: મત દર્શન આગ્રહ તજી, વર્તે સદ્ગુરુલક્ષ;
લહે શુદ્ધ સમકિત તે, જેમાં ભેદ ન પક્ષ.
link: As stated in the previous verse, the worthy soul has already attained faith in fundamental truths and the One preaching those truths, which is called vyavhar samkit.
Explaining how he attains pure faith emerging from experience of the Self which is called nishchay samkit, now the Guru says -
words: Follows the guidance of a true Guru
short: One who follows the path as directed by a true Guru, giving up insistence regarding his opinions and beliefs,
As a result he experiences the pure Self and attains experiential faith.

Irrespective of any religion, sect, caste, method or means, through which this shuddh samkit is attained, the experience of the true nature of the Self is the same for all aspirants; without any differences or divisions in it.

verses.title: State of Enlightened Self
tr: Varte nijswabhavno, anubhav laksh pratit;
Vrutti vahey nijbhavma, paramarthe samkit.
iast: Varte nijasvabhāvano, anubhava lakṣa pratīta;
Vṛtti vahe nijabhāvamāṁ, paramārthe samakita.
gu: વર્તે નિજસ્વભાવનો, અનુભવ લક્ષ પ્રતીત;
વૃત્તિ વહે નિજભાવમાં, પરમાર્થે સમકિત.
link: The aspirant embarks on the pursuit of Self-realisation in the refuge of the Sadguru.
Focusing single-pointedly on the Self, he attains shuddh samkit (experiential faith) having experienced the pure Self.
Describing the state of the one who has tasted the nectar of Self- realisation, in this verse, the Guru says -
short: Where there exists direct experience, constant awareness, firm conviction of one’s own nature,
And the tendency flows inwards;
This state is called (termed as) the highest form of right faith.

verses.title: State of Complete Dispassion
tr: Vardhaman samkit thai, taley mithyabhas;
Uday thay charitrano, vitragpada vas.
iast: Vardhamāna samakita thaī, ṭāḷe mithyābhāsa;
Udaya thāya cāritrano, vītarāgapada vāsa.
gu: વર્ધમાન સમકિત થઈ, ટાળે મિથ્યાભાસ;
ઉદય થાય ચારિત્રનો, વીતરાગપદ વાસ.
link: From verses 109 - 111, the Guru described the nature of vyavhar and nishchay samkit, as well as provided a glimpse into the inner state of a Self-realised soul.
Now in this verse, He explains how the fruit of Self-realisation - the state of dispassion is attained. The Guru says -
words: Attains state of dispassion / non-attachment / detached
short: As the state of right faith gets intensified, all feelings under the influence of deluding (mohniya) karma, that is passions and aversions, get destroyed gradually;
With the advent of right conduct, one abides in the state of complete dispassion.

verses.title: Attainment of Omniscience
tr: Keval nijswabhavnu, akhand varte jnan;
Kahie kevaljnan te, deh chhata nirvan.
iast: Kevaḷa nijasvabhāvanuṁ, akhaṁḍa varte jñāna;
Kahīe kevaḷajñāna te, deha chatāṁ nirvāṇa.
gu: કેવળ નિજસ્વભાવનું, અખંડ વર્તે જ્ઞાન;
કહીએ કેવળજ્ઞાન તે, દેહ છતાં નિર્વાણ.
link: The state of dispassion results in the unblemished, pure, constant, complete state of omniscience.
Demystifying the extraordinary essence of the nature of omniscience,  the Guru says -
words: In spite of the presence of the body
short: When there is uninterrupted constant absorption in one’s nature only,
It is known as omniscience;
In spite of the association of the body, it is known as a liberated state.

verses.title: Delusion of Infinity Vanishes on Awakening
tr: Koti varshnu swapna pan, jagrut thata shamay;
Tem vibhav anadino, jnan thata dur thay.
iast: Koṭi varṣanuṁ svapna paṇa, jāgrata thatāṁ śamāya;
Tema vibhāva anādino, jñāna thatāṁ dūra thāya.
gu: કોટિ વર્ષનું સ્વપ્ન પણ, જાગ્રત થતાં શમાય;
તેમ વિભાવ અનાદિનો, જ્ઞાન થતાં દૂર થાય.
link: After explaining the stages of spiritual progress, the Guru begins the third group of verses (114 - 118) which are inspirational, relating to the attainment of perfect purity. 2) The soul has been engaging in feelings contrary to its true nature, since time immemorial. 3) Citing a simple example to briefly answer how such impure feelings of infinite past can be eliminated and how long would it take to eliminate them, the Guru says -
words: As soon as right knowledge is attained
short: As a dream of millions of years vanishes as soon as one awakens,
Similarly delusion prevailing since infinity, vanishes as one attains enlightenment.

verses.title: Essence of True Religion
tr: Chhute dehadhyas to, nahi karta tu karma;
Nahi bhokta tu tehno, e j dharmano marma.
iast: Chūṭe dehādhyāsa to, nahi kartā tuṁ karma;
Nahi bhoktā tuṁ tehano, e ja dharmano marma.
gu: છૂટે દેહાધ્યાસ તો, નહિ કર્તા તું કર્મ;
નહિ ભોક્તા તું તેહનો, એ જ ધર્મનો મર્મ.
link: Having explained in a perfect and simple manner that one does not require infinite time to annihilate delusion of infinity, now presenting 3 mystical verses (115 - 117) which can be considered as the pinnacle like verses of this shastra.
Illuminating the essence of dharma in the first of the three mystical verses, the Guru says -
short: On renouncing the false identification with the body you no longer remain the doer of karmas nor the endurer of its fruits;
This is the essence of religion.

verses.title: Only This Religion Leads to Liberation
tr: E j dharmathi moksh chhe, tu chho moksh swaroop;
Anant darshan jnan tu, avyabadh swaroop.
iast: E ja dharmathī mokṣa che, tuṁ cho mokṣa svarūpa;
Anaṁta darśana jñāna tuṁ, avyābādha svarūpa.
gu: એ જ ધર્મથી મોક્ષ છે, તું છો મોક્ષ સ્વરૂપ;
અનંત દર્શન જ્ઞાન તું, અવ્યાબાધ સ્વરૂપ.
link: The effort to retreat from impure feelings and become established in the true nature of the Self alone is dharma.
Thus, implicitly stating that dharma is dependent on the Self, now in the next two pinnacle-like verses, the Guru describes the nature of the Self. He says -
words: Only that religion leads to liberation
You are infinite perception and knowledge
short: Only that religion as mentioned in the previous verse, leads to liberation.
As pure Self, you are liberation itself.
You are infinite perception and knowledge.
You are of unobstructed nature.

verses.title: Splendour of Soul
tr: Shuddh buddh chaitanyaghan, swayamjyoti sukhdham;
Biju kahie ketalu? Kar vichar to paam.
iast: Śuddha buddha caitanyaghana, svayamjyoti sukhadhāma;
Bījuṁ kahīe keṭaluṁ? Kara vicāra to pāma.
gu: શુદ્ધ બુદ્ધ ચૈતન્યઘન, સ્વયમ્જ્યોતિ સુખધામ;
બીજું કહીએ કેટલું? કર વિચાર તો પામ.
link: Now, in this verse, the Guru describes more qualities of the soul.
Defining the nature of the soul through five wondrous attributes, He says -
short: You are pure, knowledgeable, full of consciousness, self-luminous and the abode of bliss.
What more should I say to you?
Contemplate deeply and realise your Self.

verses.title: Universal Message of All Enlightened Ones
tr: Nishchay sarve jnanino, avi atra samay;
Dhari maunta em kahi, sahajsamadhi mai.
iast: Niścaya sarve jñānīno, āvī atra samāya;
Dharī maunatā ema kahī, sahajasamādhi māṁya.
gu: નિશ્ચય સર્વે જ્ઞાનીનો, આવી અત્ર સમાય;
ધરી મૌનતા એમ કહી, સહજસમાધિ માંય.
link: In 21 verses, through the Guru, Param Krupalu Dev conveyed the fundamental nature of the path to liberation, a complete continuous  sequence of attaining it and three mystical pinnacle-like verses.
Now, in this verse 118, He concludes the dialogue between the Guru and the disciple that had commenced in verse 45.
In this last verse that is addressed to the disciple, the Guru says -
short: The conclusion of all the Enlightened Ones has been encompassed here.
Having said this, the Guru assumes silence and enters into effortless Self-absorption.

verses.title: Disciple’s Attainment of Enlightenment
tr: Sadguruna updeshthi, avyu apurva bhan;
Nijpada nijmahi lahyu, dur thayu ajnan.
iast: Sadgurunā upadeśathī, āvyuṁ apūrva bhāna;
Nijapada nijamāṁhī lahyuṁ, dūra thayuṁ ajñāna.
gu: સદ્ગુરુના ઉપદેશથી, આવ્યું અપૂર્વ ભાન;
નિજપદ નિજમાંહી લહ્યું, દૂર થયું અજ્ઞાન.
link: In this section ‘Expression of disciple’s Enlightenment’, Param Krupalu Dev gives an amazing heart-touching account of the disciple’s state after attaining Self-realisation as well as his feeling of devotion towards the benevolent Guru.
Immersed in the feeling of gratitude, expressing his attainment of Enlightenment, the worthy disciple says -
words: By teachings of the Enlightened Mentor
short: By the teachings of the true Guru,
I realised my true Self within, which I had never experienced before,
And my self-delusive ignorance was destroyed.

verses.title: Experienced Himself as Pure Consciousness
tr: Bhasyu nijswaroop te, shuddha chetnaroop;
Ajar, amar, avinashi ne, dehatit swaroop.
iast: Bhāsyuṁ nijasvarūpa te, śuddha cetanārūpa;
Ajara, amara, avināśī ne, dehātīta svarūpa.
gu: ભાસ્યું નિજસ્વરૂપ તે, શુદ્ધ ચેતનારૂપ;
અજર, અમર, અવિનાશી ને, દેહાતીત સ્વરૂપ.
link: Through the Guru’s solutions, the disciple gained doubtless conviction regarding the six fundamental truths resulting in his experiencing the Self.
The knowledge, which till now functioned as wrong knowledge, turned into right knowledge.
Expressing how he has perceived his nature on attaining right knowledge, the disciple says -
short: I now experience my Self as pure consciousness which is ageless, immortal, indestructible and distinct from the body. (Free from old age, death and destruction.)

verses.title: Experiences Himself as Non-Doer of Karma
tr: Karta bhokta karmano, vibhav varte jyay;
Vrutti vahi nij bhaavma, thayo akarta tyay.
iast: Kartā bhoktā karmano, vibhāva varte jyāṁya;
Vṛtti vahī nijabhāvamāṁ, thayo akartā tyāṁya.
gu: કર્તા ભોક્તા કર્મનો, વિભાવ વર્તે જ્યાંય;
વૃત્તિ વહી નિજભાવમાં, થયો અકર્તા ત્યાંય.
link: The disciple stated that he was convinced regarding the first 2 fundamental truths - the soul’s existence and eternal nature.
Now in verses 121 and 122, he conveys the conviction he has gained regarding the third and fourth fundamental truth, that is, the soul being the doer and enjoyer of karma.
Describing how the soul’s doership and enjoyership modifies after the advent of Self-realisation, the disciple says -
short: The soul is the doer and the enjoyer of karma as long as there is delusion.
When the attentiveness flowed towards my own Self, I became the non-doer of the karma. (Also non-enjoyer of its fruits.)

verses.title: Doer and Enjoyer of Pure State
tr: Athva nijparinam je, shuddha chetnaroop;
Karta bhokta tehno, nirvikalp swaroop.
iast: Athavā nijapariṇāma je, śuddha cetanārūpa;
Kartā bhoktā tehano, nirvikalpa svarūpa.
gu: અથવા નિજપરિણામ જે, શુદ્ધ ચેતનારૂપ;
કર્તા ભોક્તા તેહનો, નિર્વિકલ્પ સ્વરૂપ.
link: When the tendencies flow towards one’s own pure nature, the soul becomes the non-doer and non-enjoyer of impure feelings and material karma.
Despite this, it is certainly the doer and enjoyer of the pure modifications.
The fact has been explained in this verse -
short: Alternately it may be said that,
I became the doer and enjoyer of my own modifications which are of the nature of pure consciousness without any thought activity.

verses.title: Liberation and its Path
tr: Moksh kahyo nijshuddhata, te pamey te panth;
Samjavyo sankshepma, sakal marg nirgranth.
iast: Mokṣa kahyo nijaśuddhatā, te pāme te paṁtha;
Samajāvyo saṁkṣepamāṁ, sakaḷa mārga nirgraṁtha.
gu: મોક્ષ કહ્યો નિજશુદ્ધતા, તે પામે તે પંથ;
સમજાવ્યો સંક્ષેપમાં, સકળ માર્ગ નિર્ગ્રંથ.
link: Now the worthy disciple, narrates how the Guru had explained and how he has understood the last 2 fundamental truths of the soul - ‘there is liberation’ and ‘there is a path of liberation’. The disciple says -
words: By which you achieve this state
short: Liberation is the pure state of one’s own Self,
The way it is attained is the path.
The entire path of the disentangled Lord,
Has been explained in brief.

verses.title: Disciple’s Gratitude Towards Guru
tr: Aho! Aho! Shri Sadguru, karunasindhu apar;
Aa pamar par Prabhu karyo, aho! Aho! Upkar.
iast: Aho! Aho! Śrī Sadguru, karuṇāsiṁdhu apāra;
Ā pāmara para Prabhu karyo, Aho! Aho! Upakāra.
gu: અહો! અહો! શ્રી સદ્ગુરુ, કરુણાસિંધુ અપાર;
આ પામર પર પ્રભુ કર્યો, અહો! અહો! ઉપકાર.
link: In verses 119 - 123, Param Krupalu Dev has imparted the essence of the understanding of the 6 fundamental truths in the form of the disciple narrating his own experience.
Now from verses 124 to 127, the worthy disciple expresses his gratitude towards the Guru with immense exhilaration for His great compassion.
In the first of these verses, the disciple says -
short: O! O! The great Enlightened Guru, unfathomable ocean of compassion;
On this worthless being,
O Lord! You have done the immense benevolence.

verses.title: Offers Himself at Guru’s Feet
tr: Shu Prabhucharan kaney dharu, atmathi sau heen;
Te to Prabhue apiyo, vartu charanadheen.
iast: Śuṁ Prabhucaraṇa kane dharuṁ, ātmāthī sau hīna;
Te to Prabhue āpiyo, vartuṁ caraṇādhīna.
gu: શું પ્રભુચરણ કને ધરું, આત્માથી સૌ હીન;
તે તો પ્રભુએ આપિયો, વર્તું ચરણાધીન.
link: As the worthy disciple wishes to reciprocate the supreme benevolence bestowed upon him by the Guru, he now ponders over how he could possibly do so.
In a humble expression of offering at the Lotus Feet of the Guru, the disciple says -
words: What can I offer at Your Feet
Which the Lord has given me
short: O Lord! What can I offer at Your Lotus Feet in return of Your immense benefaction?
Everything in this world is inferior than the soul.
The soul itself (i.e. Self-realisation) has been bestowed upon me by You.
Thus, it being impossible for me to offer anything, I firmly decide to live at Your command for the rest of my life.

verses.title: Sense of Servitude
tr: Aa dehadi aajthi, varto Prabhu adheen;
Das, das hu das chhu, teh Prabhuno deen.
iast: Ā dehādi ājathī, varto Prabhu ādhīna;
Dāsa, dāsa huṁ dāsa chuṁ, teha Prabhuno dīna.
gu: આ દેહાદિ આજથી, વર્તો પ્રભુ આધીન;
દાસ, દાસ હું દાસ છું, તેહ પ્રભુનો દીન.
link: The humble disciple has harboured the wish to offer everything of his at the Lotus Feet and lead a surrendered life.
In this verse, strengthening the desire to live as per His will, the disciple says -
short: From now onwards, let this body etc. be employed in the service of the Lord.
Let me be a servant, a humble servant, the most humble servant of the Lord.

verses.title: Guru’s Benevolence is Immeasurable
tr: Shat sthanak samjavine, bhinna batavyo Aap;
Myan thaki tarvarvat, e upkar amaap.
iast: Ṣaṭ sthānaka samajāvīne, bhinna batāvyo āpa;
Myāna thakī taravāravat, e upakāra amāpa.
gu: ષટ્ સ્થાનક સમજાવીને, ભિન્ન બતાવ્યો આપ;
મ્યાન થકી તરવારવત્, એ ઉપકાર અમાપ.
link: Again and again, reminiscing the boundless grace of the Guru, the disciple’s heart overflows with reverence.
Expressing the nature of the Guru’s benevolence, in the concluding verse of this section as well as the dialogue between the Guru and the disciple, he says -
words: You have explained the separateness of the soul from the body
short: By Your convincing teachings regarding the six fundamental truths,
You have revealed to me the nature of my Self, distinct and different from the body as the sword from the sheath.
This is Your immeasurable favour to me.

verses.title: Doubtless Conviction on Contemplation
tr: Darshan shatey samay chhe, aa shat sthanak mahi;
Vicharta vistarthi, sanshay rahey na kai.
iast: Upasaṁhāra Darśana ṣaṭe samāya che, ā ṣaṭ sthānaka māṁhī;
Vicāratāṁ vistārathī, saṁśaya rahe na kaṁī.
gu: ઉપસંહાર દર્શન ષટે સમાય છે, આ ષટ્ સ્થાનક માંહી;
વિચારતાં વિસ્તારથી, સંશય રહે ન કંઈ.
link: In verse 42, Param Krupalu Dev had said that He would state the six fundamentals of the soul in the form of a dialogue between a Guru and a disciple, so that the path of liberation could be understood.
Furthermore, in verse 44, He had stated that the purposeful spiritual discussion of the six schools of philosophy is encompassed within these six fundamentals.
In accordance with that, through the dialogue between the Guru and the disciple, Param Krupalu Dev expounded the six fundamental truths which pervade the six schools of philosophy.
Now concluding this subject, Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: All the six schools of philosophy are encompassed in these six fundamental truths.
No doubt can remain if one contemplates them in detail.
Vicharta = On contemplation
Vistarthi = At length
Sanshay = Doubt
Rahey = Remains
Na = Not
Kai = Any

verses.title: Remedy of Spiritual Ailment
tr: Atmabhranti sam rog nahi, Sadguru vaidya sujaan;
Guruajna sam pathya nahi, aushadh vichar dhyan.
iast: Ātmabhrāṁti sama roga nahi, Sadguru vaidya sujāṇa;
Guruājñā sama pathya nahi, auṣadha vicāra dhyāna.
gu: આત્મભ્રાંતિ સમ રોગ નહિ, સદ્ગુરુ વૈદ્ય સુજાણ;
ગુરુઆજ્ઞા સમ પથ્ય નહિ, ઔષધ વિચાર ધ્યાન.
link: In this verse, Param Krupalu Dev describes the disease of self-delusion and its remedy.
He has beautifully portrayed this through the analogy of treating a disease. Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: There is no disease like self-delusion.
An Enlightened Mentor is an expert physician capable of curing this disease.
There is no regimen like the instructions of the Guru.
The only medicine is contemplation and meditation upon the true Self.
Guru = Mentor
Ajna = Commands
Sam = Like
Pathya = Dietary restrictions
Nahi = No
Aushadh = Medicine
Vichar = Contemplation
Dhyan = Meditation

verses.title: Strive Hard for Supreme Goal
tr: Jo iccho parmarth toh, karo satya purusharth;
Bhavsthiti adi naam lai, chhedo nahi atmarth.
iast: Jo iccho paramārtha to, karo satya puruṣārtha;
Bhavasthiti ādi nāma laī, chedo nahi ātmārtha.
gu: જો ઇચ્છો પરમાર્થ તો, કરો સત્ય પુરુષાર્થ;
ભવસ્થિતિ આદિ નામ લઈ, છેદો નહિ આત્માર્થ.
link: In this concluding section, Param Krupalu Dev has composed several profound verses to iterate the grave flaws one commits, that render him incapable of curing the disease of self-delusion. So that a worthy soul can reflect upon them and make the necessary effort to eradicate them.
In the first counsel among a series of beneficial teachings given in this concluding section, inspiring one to put in the right effort, Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: If you desire to attain the supreme goal of liberation, then put in the right effort.
Do not block your spiritual progress by using excuses such as time, fate, destiny, etc.
Bhavsthiti = Destiny
Adi = Etc.
Naam = Name
Lai = Taking
Chhedo = Destroy
Nahi = Not
Atmarth = Spiritual welfare

verses.title: Attain Goal with Right Balance
tr: Nishchayvani sambhli, sadhan tajva no’y;
Nishchay rakhi lakshama, sadhan karva soy.
iast: Niścayavāṇī sāmbhaḷī, sādhana tajavāṁ no’ya;
Niścaya rākhī lakṣamāṁ, sādhana karavāṁ soya.
gu: નિશ્ચયવાણી સામ્ભળી, સાધન તજવાં નો’ય;
નિશ્ચય રાખી લક્ષમાં, સાધન કરવાં સોય.
link: Having given clear guidance to those who are bereft of right effort in verse 130, now in verses 131-134, Param Krupalu Dev points out the flaw in harbouring one-sided beliefs.
He states that only an outlook which integrates the absolute and relative viewpoints will be beneficial on the path of liberation.
This verse is addressed to those who one-sidedly adopt the absolute viewpoint and have turned away from the path of liberation.
The guidance to steer them towards the path has been given here. Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: Upon listening to the statements regarding the Self from the absolute viewpoint, one should not give up the means of attaining it.
The means should be pursued, keeping the absolute viewpoint in mind.
Nishchay = Absolute
viewpoint
Rakhi = Keeping
Lakshama = In focus
Sadhan = Means
Karva = Do
Soy = That

verses.title: Integrating Both Viewpoints
tr: Naya nishchay ekantthi, ama nathi kahel;
Ekante vyavhar nahi, banne sath rahel.
iast: Naya niścaya ekāṁtathī, āmāṁ nathī kahela;
Ekāṁte vyavahāra nahi, banne sātha rahela.
gu: નય નિશ્ચય એકાંતથી, આમાં નથી કહેલ;
એકાંતે વ્યવહાર નહિ, બન્ને સાથ રહેલ.
link: The path of liberation is the combination of the awareness of the pure Self and right conduct.
However, it is often observed that seekers are unable to maintain a balance of both and, hence cannot progress on the path of liberation.
In order to emphasise that the goal of liberation cannot be accomplished by pursuing it with a one-sided approach, in this verse Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: Here, in this scripture, the account has not been given from the one-sided view of the absolute standpoint or the one-sided view of the relative standpoint.
The harmony of both the standpoints has been kept in view.
Ekante = One-sidedly
Vyavhar = Relative viewpoint
Nahi = Not
Banne = Both
Sath = Together
Rahel = Present

verses.title: Essence of Spiritual Pursuit
tr: Gacchmatni je kalpana, te nahi sadvyavhar;
Bhan nahi nijroopnu, te nishchay nahi saar.
iast: Gacchamatanī je kalpanā, te nahi sadvyavahāra;
Bhāna nahīṁ nijarūpanuṁ, te niścaya nahi sāra.
gu: ગચ્છમતની જે કલ્પના, તે નહિ સદ્વ્યવહાર;
ભાન નહીં નિજરૂપનું, તે નિશ્ચય નહિ સાર.
link: Describing those who wrongly adopt the relative viewpoint and those who are deluded regarding the absolute viewpoint, Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: Sectarian views and imaginary opinions of religious orders do not constitute the right practice.
In the same way, where there is no awareness of one’s pure Self, the knowledge from the absolute standpoint is futile.

verses.title: The Path in All Times
tr: Agal Jnani thai gaya, vartamanma hoy;
Thashe kaal bhavishyama, margbhed nahi koy.
iast: Āgaḷa jñānī thaī gayā, vartamānamāṁ hoya;
Thāśe kāḷa bhaviṣyamāṁ, mārgabheda nahi koya.
gu: આગળ જ્ઞાની થઈ ગયા, વર્તમાનમાં હોય;
થાશે કાળ ભવિષ્યમાં, માર્ગભેદ નહિ કોય.
link: Shedding light on the path of supreme truth, Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: All the Enlightened Ones of the past, present and future have attained, do attain and will attain liberation in the same way; there is no difference in the path.
It is definite and undisputable in all three periods of time.

verses.title: Two Causes of Liberation
tr: Sarva jiva chhe Siddh sam, je samje te thay;
Sadguruajna Jindasha, nimit karan mai.
iast: Sarva jīva che siddha sama, je samaje te thāya;
Sadguruājñā Jinadaśā, nimitta kāraṇa māṁya.
gu: સર્વ જીવ છે સિદ્ધ સમ, જે સમજે તે થાય;
સદ્ગુરુઆજ્ઞા જિનદશા, નિમિત્ત કારણ માંય.
link: From verses 131-134, Param Krupalu Dev demonstrated that the path of supreme truth is the integration of the absolute and relative viewpoints.
He pointed out a significant fact that there is no spiritual benefit in holding on to one-sided beliefs.
Now, in verses 135-136, He states that the path of liberation is the acceptance of both the principal and instrumental causes. Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: All souls by nature are like the Liberated Ones.
The one who realises this fact becomes liberated.
The commands of a true Guru and the pure state of the Omniscient Ones are the instrumental causes of this.
Sadguruajna = Commands of Enlightened Mentor
Jindasha = State of Omniscient One
Nimit = Instrumental
Karan = Causes
Mai = Are

verses.title: Forsaking One Cause is Fatal
tr: Upadannu naam lai, e je taje nimit;
Pamey nahi siddhatvane, rahey bhrantima sthit.
iast: Upādānanuṁ nāma laī, e je taje nimitta;
Pāme nahi siddhatvane, rahe bhrāṁtimāṁ sthita.
gu: ઉપાદાનનું નામ લઈ, એ જે તજે નિમિત્ત;
પામે નહિ સિદ્ધત્વને, રહે ભ્રાંતિમાં સ્થિત.
link: Explaining what fate awaits those who adopt only the principal cause and disregard the contribution of the instrumental causes, Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: Putting forward the principal cause, one who abandons the instrumental cause does not attain liberation, remaining entangled in delusion.
Pamey = Attains
Nahi = Not
Siddhatvane = Liberation
Rahey = Remains
Bhrantima = In delusion
Sthit = Established

verses.title: Hypocrites Betray Enlightened Ones
tr: Mukhthi jnan kathe ane, antar chhutyo na moh;
Te pamar prani karey, matra Jnanino droh.
iast: Mukhathī jñāna kathe ane, aṁtar chūṭyo na moha;
Te pāmara prāṇī kare, mātra jñānīno droha.
gu: મુખથી જ્ઞાન કથે અને, અંતર્ છૂટ્યો ન મોહ;
તે પામર પ્રાણી કરે, માત્ર જ્ઞાનીનો દ્રોહ.
link: In verse 136, Param Krupalu Dev illustrated the state of the dry intellectualist, who one-sidedly holds the absolute viewpoint.
Now, clearly depicting the offence of the dry intellectualist, Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: One who engages in lofty discussions of knowledge, despite internally possessing strong delusion, is a hypocrite.
Such a wretched one only betrays the Enlightened Ones.
Te = That
Pamar = Wretched
Prani = Being
Karey = Does
Matra = Only
Jnanino = Towards Enlightened Ones
Droh = Betrayal

verses.title: Seven Cardinal Virtues of Seeker
tr: Daya, shanti, samta, kshama, satya, tyag, vairagya;
Hoy mumukshu ghat vishe, eh saday sujagya.
iast: Dayā, śāṁti, samatā, kṣamā, satya, tyāga, vairāgya;
Hoya mumukṣu ghaṭa viṣe, eha sadāya sujāgya.
gu: દયા, શાંતિ, સમતા, ક્ષમા, સત્ય, ત્યાગ, વૈરાગ્ય;
હોય મુમુક્ષુ ઘટ વિષે, એહ સદાય સુજાગ્ય.
link: One who engages in lofty speeches of knowledge despite possessing strong delusion within, is certainly not an Enlightened One. He is not even worthy of being called a true seeker.
Portraying the virtues that adorn a true seeker, that is, the qualities which have blossomed in one desirous of liberation, Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: Compassion, tranquillity, equanimity, forgiveness, truthfulness, renunciation, detachment are qualities that are constantly awake in the heart of an aspirant of liberation.
Hoy = Are
Mumukshu = Desirous of liberation
Ghat = Heart
Vishe = In
Eh = These
Saday = Constantly
Sujagya = Vigilant

verses.title: Enlightened One and Verbal Intellectualist
tr: Mohbhaav kshay hoy jya, athva hoy prashant;
Te kahiye Jnanidasha, baki kahiye bhrant.
iast: Mohabhāva kṣaya hoya jyāṁ, athavā hoya praśāṁta;
Te kahīe jñānīdaśā, bākī kahīe bhrāṁta.
gu: મોહભાવ ક્ષય હોય જ્યાં, અથવા હોય પ્રશાંત;
તે કહીએ જ્ઞાનીદશા, બાકી કહીએ ભ્રાંત.
link: In the previous verse, describing the virtues of a true seeker in seven words, Param Krupalu Dev portrayed a mumukshu.
Now in verses 139 and 140, He describes the attributes of an Enlightened One. In this verse Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: Where delusion has been destroyed or has subsided, that is the state of an Enlightened One.
All others are in illusion.
Te = That
Kahiye = Is called
Jnanidasha = Enlightened state
Baki = All else
Kahiye = Is called
Bhrant = Illusion

verses.title: How World Appears to Enlightened Ones
tr: Sakal jagat te ethvat, athva swapna saman;
Te kahiye Jnanidasha, baki vachajnan.
iast: Sakaḷa jagata te eṭhavat, athavā svapna samāna;
Te kahīe jñānīdaśā, bākī vācājñāna.
gu: સકળ જગત તે એઠવત્, અથવા સ્વપ્ન સમાન;
તે કહીએ જ્ઞાનીદશા, બાકી વાચાજ્ઞાન.
link: The difference between an Enlightened One and a verbal intellectualist became clearly visible in the previous verse.
Describing two analogies regarding how the world appears to an Enlightened One, Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: When the whole world appears like leftover food or like a dream, that is considered the enlightened state.
Otherwise it is mere verbal knowledge.

verses.title: Result of Studying This Scripture
tr: Sthanak panch vicharine, chhatthe varte jeh;
Pamey sthanak panchmu, ema nahi sandeh.
iast: Sthānaka pāṁca vicārīne, chaṭhṭhe varte jeha;
Pāme sthānaka pāṁcamuṁ, emāṁ nahi saṁdeha.
gu: સ્થાનક પાંચ વિચારીને, છઠ્ઠે વર્તે જેહ;
પામે સ્થાનક પાંચમું, એમાં નહિ સંદેહ.
link: Describing the nature of the Enlightened One, which can clearly be differentiated from the verbal intellectualist, Param Krupalu Dev brought this subject to a close.
Before completing Shri Atmasiddhi Shastra, He shows what one should do after studying this scripture. Param Krupalu Dev says -
short: Contemplating over the five aphorisms, if one acts according to the sixth, which is the path of liberation; he will attain the fifth, which is liberation.
There is no doubt about it.
Pamey = Attains
Sthanak = Abode
Panchmu = Fifth
Ema = In that
Nahi = No
Sandeh = Doubt

verses.title: Innumerable Salutations to Enlightened One
tr: Deh chhata jeni dasha, varte dehatit;
Te Jnanina charanma, ho vandan aganit.
iast: Deha chatāṁ jenī daśā, varte dehātīta;
Te jñānīnā caraṇamāṁ, ho vaṁdana agaṇita.
gu: દેહ છતાં જેની દશા, વર્તે દેહાતીત;
તે જ્ઞાનીના ચરણમાં, હો વંદન અગણિત.
link: Just as authors commence a scripture in an auspicious manner by offering obeisance to their revered deity, they also conclude the scripture by bowing to their venerable Lord. This stems from the satisfaction of completing the text without any hindrance. It is an expression of gratitude.
In keeping with this ancient tradition, with a heart full of devotion, Param Krupalu Dev concludes -
short: My innumerable salutations at the Lotus Feet of that Enlightened One, whose state of existence is beyond the body, though in an embodied condition.

iast: Patita jana pāvanī, sura saritā samī,
Adhama uddhāriṇī ātmasiddhi,
Janma janmāṁtaro jāṇatā jogīe,
Ātmaanubhava vaḍe āja dīdhī;
Bhakta Bhagīratha samā, bhāgyaśāḷī mahā,
Bhavya Saubhāgyanī vinatithī,
Cārutara bhūminā nagara Naḍiyādamāṁ,
Pūrṇa kṛpā Prabhue karī’tī. Patita.
gu: પતિત જન પાવની, સુર સરિતા સમી,
અધમ ઉદ્ધારિણી આત્મસિદ્ધિ,
જન્મ જન્માંતરો જાણતા જોગીએ,
આત્મઅનુભવ વડે આજ દીધી;
ભક્ત ભગીરથ સમા, ભાગ્યશાળી મહા,
ભવ્ય સૌભાગ્યની વિનતિથી,
ચારુતર ભૂમિના નગર નડિયાદમાં,
પૂર્ણ કૃપા પ્રભુએ કરી’તી. પતિત.

iast: Yāda nadīnī dhare, nāma Naḍiyāda paṇa,
Caraṇa cūmī mahāpuruṣonā,
Paramakṛpāḷunī caraṇaraja saṁtanī,
Bhaktibhūmi hare citta saunā;
Samīpa rahī eka Aṁbālāle tahīṁ,
Bhakti karī dīpa hāthe dharīne,
Ekī kalame karī pūrī Kṛpāḷue,
Āso Vada ekame ’siddhijīne. Patita.
gu: યાદ નદીની ધરે, નામ નડિયાદ પણ,
ચરણ ચૂમી મહાપુરુષોના,
પરમકૃપાળુની ચરણરજ સંતની,
ભક્તિભૂમિ હરે ચિત્ત સૌના;
સમીપ રહી એક અંબાલાલે તહીં,
ભક્તિ કરી દીપ હાથે ધરીને,
એકી કલમે કરી પૂરી કૃપાળુએ,
આસો વદ એકમે ’સિદ્ધિજીને. પતિત.
